<|start|>user<|message|>A wildfire drone surveillance swarm shares a single satellite downlink channel that only one drone may transmit on at a time. Incoming imagery tasks pile into a bounded work queue; drones enqueue new tasks only while the queue has room, and the ground station drains tasks one at a time. Because smoke conditions vary, the operator can reconfigure the queue capacity up or down at runtime, but never below the number of tasks already waiting. A drone grabs the downlink only when it is free and releases it when its burst finishes. The safety concern is that two drones must never be transmitting on the shared downlink simultaneously.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at no reachable state do two drones hold the shared downlink channel at the same time.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od14m4p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers
VARIABLES holders, queue, cap
Init == holders = 0 /\ queue = 0 /\ cap = 2
Grab == holders = 0 /\ holders' = (holders) + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, cap>>
Release == holders > 0 /\ holders' = holders - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, cap>>
Enqueue == queue < cap /\ queue' = queue + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, cap>>
Drain == queue > 0 /\ queue' = queue - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, cap>>
Reconfig == \E c \in {2, 3} : c >= queue /\ cap' = c /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, queue>>
Next == Grab \/ Release \/ Enqueue \/ Drain \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<holders, queue, cap>>
ExclusiveDownlink == holders >= 0 /\ holders <= 1 /\ queue >= 0 /\ queue <= cap
====
```
```cfg
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ExclusiveDownlink
```<|return|>

<|start|>user<|message|>A wildfire drone surveillance swarm writes consolidated maps to a shared store using optimistic locking with retry. Each write carries the epoch the drone believes is current; the store bumps its epoch on every accepted write, and the operator may grow the mission's epoch capacity at runtime as new drones join. A drone reads the store epoch, prepares a write, then commits only if its cached epoch still equals the store epoch, otherwise it retries with a fresh read. The count of accepted writes must always equal the store epoch, because every accepted write advances the epoch exactly once. The hazard is a stale drone committing under an old epoch and silently overwriting newer data.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of accepted writes always equals the store's current epoch, so no stale-epoch write is ever accepted.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od14m0p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers
VARIABLES epoch, accepted, cachedOk
Init == epoch = 0 /\ accepted = 0 /\ cachedOk = FALSE
Read == cachedOk' = TRUE /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, accepted>>
Commit == cachedOk = TRUE /\ epoch < 4 /\ epoch' = (epoch) + 1 /\ accepted' = accepted + 1 /\ cachedOk' = FALSE
Stale == cachedOk = FALSE /\ cachedOk' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, accepted>>
Next == Read \/ Commit \/ Stale
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<epoch, accepted, cachedOk>>
OnlyCurrentEpochWrites == accepted = epoch
====
```
```cfg
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OnlyCurrentEpochWrites
```<|return|>

<|start|>user<|message|>An elevator bank in a skyscraper routes waiting passengers through a bounded dispatch queue with backpressure: passengers move from the lobby pool into cars, and cars later discharge them at their floors, but no passenger is ever created or lost in transit. New boarding requests are admitted only while a car has spare room. One car controller can crash silently and simply stop accepting boardings, but the passengers it already holds remain accounted for. Across every step the total number of people equals those still in the lobby plus those currently riding. The safety concern is strict conservation of people.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the count of people in the lobby plus the count riding in cars always equals the fixed building population.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od6m4p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers
VARIABLES lobby, riding, alive
Init == lobby = 3 /\ riding = 0 /\ alive = TRUE
Board == alive /\ lobby > 0 /\ riding < 3 /\ lobby' = lobby - 1 /\ riding' = (riding) + 1 /\ UNCHANGED alive
Discharge == riding > 0 /\ riding' = riding - 1 /\ lobby' = lobby + 1 /\ UNCHANGED alive
Crash == alive /\ alive' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, riding>>
Idle == UNCHANGED <<lobby, riding, alive>>
Next == Board \/ Discharge \/ Crash \/ Idle
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<lobby, riding, alive>>
PassengerConservation == lobby + riding = 3
====
```
```cfg
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PassengerConservation
```<|return|>

<|start|>user<|message|>A smart-home door-lock network elects a leader hub to issue the single irreversible master-unlock pulse for the front door; if the leader fails, a standby is elected to take over. The number of provisioned hubs can grow at runtime as the household adds devices. Only the current leader may fire the unlock, and once the door has been unlocked that irreversible pulse must never be issued a second time in the session. Leadership can hand off, but the fired flag persists across handoffs. The safety concern is that the irreversible unlock happens at most once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the master-unlock pulse is fired at most once across the whole session, regardless of leader failover.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla

<|start|>user<|message|>An airport baggage router elects one leader controller to divert bags onto the sortation belt; a standby is elected on failover. Two independent baggage systems share one physical belt pool, so their leaders are drawn from a common set of controller ids, and a diversion is authorized only when it comes from the controller that is currently the leader. A stale controller that believes it is still leader must never route a bag. Every routed bag increments the count of authorized routings, which must never exceed the count of diversions the true leader performed. The hazard is a deposed controller routing bags it is no longer authorized to route.

<|start|>user<|message|>A print-shop job spooler grants exclusive press access with a token ring: the print token circulates among stations, and only the station currently holding the token may claim the next open output slot. One station can be slow but never fails, so the token always eventually keeps moving. Each grant advances both the claimed-slot counter and the granted counter together. The hazard is the same output slot being allocated twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of claimed slots always equals the number of grants issued, so no slot is ever double-allocated.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla

<|start|>user<|message|>A warehouse robot fleet stages totes on a shared staging shelf under epoch-numbered reconfiguration: a coordinator bumps the epoch whenever it rebalances zones, and robots carry an epoch tag on each deposit. Messages between robots and the coordinator can be reordered, so a deposit may arrive after a pickup that logically preceded it, but the shelf must never hold more totes than its fixed capacity. Robots deposit a tote only while the shelf has room and pick totes back off when routing them onward. Reconfiguration changes the epoch but not the physical shelf limit. The hazard is exceeding the bounded shelf capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of totes on the staging shelf never exceeds its fixed capacity.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla

<|start|>user<|message|>A subway signalling block system records each block's occupancy with optimistic locking and retry. A train controller reads a block's version, computes its update, and commits only if the version is unchanged, bumping the version and applying the update atomically; the number of committed updates must equal the version. The line can add signalling blocks at runtime, growing capacity. A stale commit whose read version no longer matches is rejected and retried, so no update is ever lost or applied out of order. Each accepted commit advances committed count and version together. The hazard is a lost update where the version and the applied-update count drift apart.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the count of applied block updates always equals the record's version, so no committed update is ever lost.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla

Idle == UNCHANGED <<version, applied, capacity>>
Next == Commit \/ Grow \/ Idle
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<version, applied, capacity>>

<|start|>user<|message|>A library book-reservation system tracks the fixed number of physical copies of a title using a compare-and-swap register on the availability count. A patron reserves a copy by atomically swapping the available count down and the reserved count up; returns swap the other way. No copy is ever created or destroyed, so available plus reserved always equals the total number of copies owned. One reservation agent can be slow but never fails, so a pending swap always eventually resolves. The register guarantees each swap either fully applies or not at all. The hazard is a bookkeeping error that creates or loses a copy.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of available copies plus the number of reserved copies always equals the fixed total of copies owned.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla

Each machine casts at most one vote per term, and vote messages travel over an unreliable bus that may deliver them in any order, so votes are recorded in arbitrary sequence. A candidate becomes leader only after collecting votes from a strict majority of the machines in its term. Any machine may crash, which drops it back to a plain follower and triggers a failover election, and a crashed machine may later recover as a follower. ------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m3p0t1 -------------------------

CONSTANTS Machines, MaxTerm

ASSUME MaxTerm \in Nat /\ MaxTerm >= 1

VARIABLES term, role, votedFor, votes, alive

vars == << term, role, votedFor, votes, alive >>

NoVote == "none"
Quorum == Cardinality(Machines) \div 2 + 1

Init ==
    /\ term     = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ role     = [m \in Machines |-> "follower"]
    /\ votedFor = [m \in Machines |-> NoVote]
    /\ votes    = [m \in Machines |-> {}]
    /\ alive    = [m \in Machines |-> TRUE]

StartElection(c) ==
    /\ alive[c]
    /\ term[c] < MaxTerm
    /\ term'     = [term EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
    /\ role'     = [role EXCEPT ![c] = "candidate"]
    /\ votedFor' = [votedFor EXCEPT ![c] = c]
    /\ votes'    = [votes EXCEPT ![c] = {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED alive

CastVote(v, c) ==
    /\ alive[v]
    /\ role[c] = "candidate"
    /\ term[c] >= term[v]
    /\ (term[c] > term[v] \/ votedFor[v] = NoVote)
    /\ v \notin votes[c]
    /\ term'     = [term EXCEPT ![v] = term[c]]
    /\ votedFor' = [votedFor EXCEPT ![v] = c]
    /\ role'     = [role EXCEPT ![v] = IF v = c THEN role[v] ELSE "follower"]
    /\ votes'    = [votes EXCEPT ![c] = @ \cup {v}]
    /\ UNCHANGED alive

BecomeLeader(c) ==
    /\ role[c] = "candidate"
    /\ Cardinality(votes[c]) >= Quorum
    /\ role' = [role EXCEPT ![c] = "leader"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, votedFor, votes, alive >>

Crash(m) ==
    /\ alive[m]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
    /\ role'  = [role EXCEPT ![m] = "follower"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, votedFor, votes >>

Recover(m) ==
    /\ ~alive[m]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, role, votedFor, votes >>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Machines : StartElection(c) \/ BecomeLeader(c)
    \/ \E v \in Machines, c \in Machines : CastVote(v, c)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Crash(m) \/ Recover(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OneLeaderPerTerm ==
    \A a, b \in Machines :
        (role[a] = "leader" /\ role[b] = "leader" /\ term[a] = term[b]) => a = b
=============================================================================

Quorum == Cardinality(Replicas) \div 2 + 1

    /\ held      = [p \in Printers |-> NoJob]
    /\ rvote     = [r \in Replicas |-> [p \in Printers |-> NoJob]]

        /\ held[p] = NoJob

        /\ rvote[r][pr.prn] = NoJob

        /\ UNCHANGED << assigned, held, proposals >>

  /\ holder \in Trains
  /\ passes = {}
  /\ sealed = {}
  /\ sealer = [b \in Blocks |-> None]
  /\ capacity = 1

\* The token holder releases the token as an in-flight pass to another train.
Circulate(t, u) ==
  /\ holder = t
  /\ u # t
  /\ passes' = passes \cup {[to |-> u]}
  /\ holder' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, sealer, capacity>>

\* An in-flight pass is delivered in any order, making its target the holder.
DeliverPass(m) ==
  /\ holder = None
  /\ holder' = m.to
  /\ passes' = passes \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, sealer, capacity>>

\* The irreversible action: the holder seals an as-yet-unsealed block, provided
\* the number already sealed is below the running capacity. A sealed block is
\* recorded with the train that sealed it and is never unsealed.
Seal(t, b) ==
  /\ holder = t
  /\ b \notin sealed
  /\ Cardinality(sealed) < capacity
  /\ sealed' = sealed \cup {b}
  /\ sealer' = [sealer EXCEPT ![b] = t]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, passes, capacity>>

\* The control centre may raise the running capacity up to the fixed maximum.
RaiseCapacity ==
  /\ capacity < MaxCap
  /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, passes, sealed, sealer>>

\* It may also lower capacity, but never below the count already sealed -- that
\* would demand un-sealing, which the one-way discipline forbids.
LowerCapacity ==
  /\ capacity - 1 >= Cardinality(sealed)
  /\ capacity > 0
  /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, passes, sealed, sealer>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains, u \in Trains : Circulate(t, u)
  \/ \E m \in passes : DeliverPass(m)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Seal(t, b)

  \/ LowerCapacity

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A block counts as sealed exactly when it carries a sealer of record, and the
\* sealed count never exceeds the running capacity. Because no action removes a
\* block from the sealed set or clears its sealer, each block is sealed -- the
\* irreversible act -- at most once.
SealIntegrity ==
  /\ \A b \in Blocks : (b \in sealed) <=> (sealer[b] # None)
  /\ Cardinality(sealed) <= capacity

SumOver(f, S) ==

  /\ parked = 0
  /\ nextId = 0

  /\ loc[s] > 0
  /\ d # s

  /\ nextId' = nextId + 1

TypeOK ==
    /\ stock \in 0..3
    /\ capacity \in CapLevels
    /\ ballot \in [Nodes -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ proposal \in {0} \cup Amounts
    /\ mode \in {"idle", "voting"}

Init ==
    /\ stock = 0
    /\ capacity = 2
    /\ ballot = [n \in Nodes |-> "none"]
    /\ proposal = 0
    /\ mode = "idle"

\* A clerk proposes depositing a batch of blood units into the shared stock.
Propose(a) ==
    /\ mode = "idle"
    /\ proposal' = a
    /\ mode' = "voting"
    /\ ballot' = [n \in Nodes |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, capacity>>

\* A node approves the deposit because the result fits the fridge capacity.
ApproveYes(n) ==
    /\ mode = "voting"
    /\ ballot[n] = "none"
    /\ stock + proposal <= capacity
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![n] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, capacity, proposal, mode>>

\* A node rejects the deposit because the result would exceed capacity.
ApproveNo(n) ==
    /\ mode = "voting"
    /\ ballot[n] = "none"
    /\ stock + proposal > capacity
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![n] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, capacity, proposal, mode>>

\* With a quorum of approvals the deposit is applied to the shared stock.
Commit ==
    /\ mode = "voting"
    /\ Cardinality({n \in Nodes : ballot[n] = "yes"}) >= QuorumSize
    /\ stock' = stock + proposal
    /\ proposal' = 0
    /\ mode' = "idle"
    /\ ballot' = [n \in Nodes |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED capacity

\* With a quorum of rejections the deposit is discarded.
Abort ==
    /\ mode = "voting"
    /\ Cardinality({n \in Nodes : ballot[n] = "no"}) >= QuorumSize
    /\ proposal' = 0
    /\ mode' = "idle"
    /\ ballot' = [n \in Nodes |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, capacity>>

\* A single unit is issued out, reducing the stock.
Withdraw ==
    /\ mode = "idle"
    /\ stock > 0
    /\ stock' = stock - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, ballot, proposal, mode>>

\* Fridge capacity is re-rated at runtime, never below the current stock.
Recapacitate(k) ==
    /\ mode = "idle"
    /\ k >= stock
    /\ capacity' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, ballot, proposal, mode>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Amounts : Propose(a)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : ApproveYes(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : ApproveNo(n)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ Withdraw
    \/ \E k \in CapLevels : Recapacitate(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity is never exceeded: the stored stock always stays within
\* the currently configured fridge capacity.
CapacityRespected == stock <= capacity

<|start|>user<|message|>A wildfire drone surveillance swarm allocates disjoint surveillance slots (grid cells) to drones through a two-phase-commit coordinator. When the coordinator is idle, a free drone proposes to take some slot that is not already granted, entering the voting phase (Propose). If the proposal cannot proceed the coordinator aborts it and the drone returns to idle (Abort). A drone can crash silently at any time; it stops responding and, if it was mid-proposal, the coordinator round is cleared so others can continue (Crash). No surveillance slot may ever be allocated to two different drones simultaneously.

<|start|>user<|message|>A warehouse robot fleet drains a fixed pool of jobs. Jobs start in a backlog, flow
through a bounded work queue that applies backpressure (nothing can be enqueued once
the queue is full), get carried by robots, and end up finished. A robot may be slow
but never fails outright: while slow it makes no progress, yet it never drops the job
it is carrying, so no job is ever lost or duplicated.

Actions:
- Enqueue: move one job from the backlog into the queue, only while the queue has
  room (backpressure blocks it when full).
- Pick(r): a ready robot not already carrying takes one job out of the queue.
- Complete(r): a ready robot carrying a job finishes it, incrementing the done count.
- Stall(r): a ready robot becomes slow (temporarily stops making progress).
- Resume(r): a slow robot becomes ready again, still holding any job it had.

The total number of jobs (backlog + in the queue + being carried + finished) equals a
fixed constant at all times.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the count of jobs in the backlog, in the queue, carried by robots,
and finished always sums to the fixed total.

<|start|>user<|message|>Hospital operating-room scheduler: writer clients (w1, w2) revise the shared
operating-room schedule record, which carries a version counter. Each writer uses
optimistic locking with retry: it first reads the current version, then attempts to
commit its revision only if the version it read still matches the live version. A
successful commit bumps the version and emits an apply message that folds the
writer's revision into the record; because the network reorders messages, apply
messages are held in an unordered in-flight set and may be folded in any order. If a
writer discovers its read has gone stale it abandons the attempt and retries from a
fresh read. This is exactly what stops a stale writer from silently overwriting and
losing another writer's committed revision.

Actions: Read (an idle writer records the current version), Commit (a writer whose
read is still current bumps the version and puts its apply message in flight),
Retry (a writer whose read went stale returns to re-read), Apply (fold an in-flight
apply message into the shared record), and Idle.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every writer that has committed either already has its revision folded into the record or still has its apply message in flight, so no committed revision is ever lost.

<|start|>user<|message|>Subway signalling block system: trains (t1, t2) run over track blocks (b1, b2), and a

single entry token circulates around a ring of trains; only the current token holder
may claim a block, which serializes claims. A train first requests a target block,
then, while holding the token and standing on no block, enters its requested block
only if that block is currently unoccupied. A train leaves its block to free it. A
train may crash silently: it stops participating but its block stays occupied (so it is
never double-claimed) until manually cleared by leaving. The token is passed around the
ring to give another train the chance to claim.

Actions: Request (a live train picks a target block), Enter (the token holder, standing
on no block, claims its requested unoccupied block), Leave (a train vacates its block),
Crash (a train crashes silently), Pass (the holder hands the entry token to another
train), and Idle.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any two distinct trains that are on a block are on different blocks, so no track block is ever occupied by two trains at once.

<|start|>user<|message|>A blood-bank inventory tracker feeds cross-match requests to the bench technicians. The
bank is licensed for a fixed number of open cross-matches at once, and that licence is the
capacity the tracker must never breach.

Requests arrive in an inbox and are admitted, in order, onto a bounded intake queue. A
request that has been admitted occupies one of the licensed slots, and it keeps occupying
that slot the whole time it is in the system: while it waits in the queue and also while a
technician has it on the bench. Admission is therefore refused -- this is the
backpressure -- whenever the queue length plus the number of requests currently on
benches has reached the licence. A technician takes the request at the head of the queue
onto its bench, works it, and completes the cross-match, which is when the slot is finally
given back.

A bench technician can crash silently, mid-request, with nothing announcing it. The
request on that technician's bench is not lost: the shift supervisor puts it back onto the
tail of the intake queue, which moves the slot from the bench back to the queue without
ever changing how many slots are in use. A crashed technician whose bench has been cleared
can be restarted.

Actions: the tracker admits an inbox request onto the tail of the intake queue when the
licence has room; a technician takes the head request of the queue onto its bench; a
technician completes the cross-match on its bench and gives the slot back; a technician
crashes silently; the supervisor puts a crashed technician's bench request back onto the
tail of the queue; a crashed technician with an empty bench is restarted.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of requests waiting on the intake queue plus the number of
technicians with a request on the bench never exceeds the bank's licensed number of open
cross-matches.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every request that lands on a technician's bench eventually leaves that
bench, either completed or put back on the queue, so nothing sits on a bench forever.

<|start|>user<|message|>A stock exchange opening auction is run by two completely independent matching instances
that happen to share one pool of an issue's shares. The instances have no common
scheduler and no shared book; each keeps its own opening print tally, and the only thing
that coordinates them is a token ring.

Three trading desks sit on the ring, and exactly one of them holds the ring token at any
moment. The token is what grants exclusive access to the shared pool: only the desk
holding the token may pull shares out of the pool onto its own pad. A desk hands the
token on to the next desk in ring order, but only once its own pad is empty, so a desk
never carries pulled shares across a handoff.

Shares on a desk's pad go one of two ways. They can be crossed into the opening print of
whichever instance that desk belongs to, or they can be put straight back into the shared
pool. An opening print that has already been struck can still be cancelled before the
open, which sends those shares back into the shared pool as well.

Actions: the token holder hands the token to the next desk on the ring once its pad is
empty; the token holder pulls a share out of the shared pool onto its pad; a desk crosses
a share from its pad into its own instance's opening print; a desk puts a share from its
pad back into the shared pool; an instance cancels a share from its opening print and
returns it to the shared pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shares sitting in the shared pool, plus the shares on the three
desks' pads, plus the shares crossed into the two instances' opening prints always add up
to the issue's total share count, so no pull, cross, return, or cancellation ever creates
or destroys a share.

<|start|>user<|message|>An air-traffic runway allocator works with a fixed set of physical progress strips. Every
strip is at any moment in exactly one of three places: racked in the strip bay, in a
controller's hand, or posted at one of the runways. Strips are never printed and never
shredded during a shift, so the count of them cannot change.

Controllers take strips out of the rack through one compare-and-swap allocation register.
A controller reads the register, remembering the value it saw, and may then pull a strip
out of the rack only if the register still reads exactly what it remembered; the pull
ticks the register. A read the register has already moved past is discarded and the
controller reads again. A controller holds at most one strip.

A strip in hand is either posted at a runway or racked again. Posting is only allowed at
a runway that is currently open. A strip posted at a runway comes back to the rack when
that runway's movement is complete.

Runway capacity changes through the shift: runways are closed for sweeping, inspection or
weather and are reopened afterwards. A runway may only be closed when nothing is posted at
it, so closing never strands a strip, and a closed runway can be reopened at any time.

Actions: a controller reads the allocation register; a controller whose read still matches
pulls a strip from the rack and ticks the register; a controller discards a read the
register has moved past; a controller posts the strip in its hand at an open runway; a
controller racks the strip in its hand again; a completed movement returns a posted strip
to the rack; a runway with nothing posted at it is closed; a closed runway is reopened.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The strips racked in the bay, plus the strips posted at the left and
right runways, plus the strips in controllers' hands always add up to the shift's total
strip count, so no allocation, stale-read retry, or runway closure ever creates or loses a
strip.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Any strip a controller is holding eventually leaves that controller's
hand, so no controller stands holding a strip forever.

of one of the three places only if the stamp still reads exactly what it remembered; the

away and reads again. A clerk carries at most one copy. A copy in a clerk's hands is put
down into whichever of the three places the clerk is heading for.

so with a copy still in hand. Nothing announces this. The floor porter sweeps up after a

lifts a copy out of one of the three places and ticks the stamp; a clerk throws away a
reading the stamp has overtaken; a clerk puts the copy in hand down into one of the three

stacks; a crashed, empty-handed clerk comes back on shift.

the copies out on loan, plus the copies in clerks' hands always add up to the title's total
copy count, so no move, stale-read retry, crash, or sweep ever creates or loses a copy.

<|start|>user<|message|>An airport baggage router moves a fixed set of bags from the check-in infeed to the
aircraft. A bag is at any moment in exactly one place: waiting on the infeed, riding the
bounded sortation queue, sitting in one of the two make-up chutes, or already loaded. Bags
are neither created nor destroyed by the router; a bag pulled off an aircraft for a rescan
simply goes back to the infeed.

The sortation queue is bounded and applies backpressure: while it holds its full number of
bags nothing more is admitted from the infeed, and admitted bags leave the queue in the
order they entered. A bag admitted onto the queue carries the chute it is destined for,
and when it reaches the front of the queue it drops into that chute.

Each chute is worked by a handler who lifts bags out of it and loads them. Handlers here
are slow, never failed: a handler can go slow, during which it loads nothing at all, and it
comes back up to speed on its own. Nothing is ever taken away from a slow handler and no
other handler covers its chute; the bags simply wait in the chute until the handler is
back.

queue has room; the bag at the front of the queue drops into its destination chute; a
handler that is up to speed lifts a bag out of its chute and loads it; a loaded bag is
pulled back to the infeed for a rescan; a handler goes slow; a handler comes back up to
speed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The bags waiting on the infeed, plus the bags riding the sortation queue,
plus the bags sitting in the two make-up chutes, plus the bags already loaded always add up
to the router's total bag count.

Only the round at the head of the journal is actively being voted on. While that head round is short of a full set of votes, the CollectVote step records one more fridge controller's yes vote for it. Alternatively RefuseHead may fire while the head round is still short of a full set of votes: a controller declines, the round is discarded from the journal, its vote tally resets and the owning instance returns to idle. Once the head round has collected a vote from every controller, it resolves in one of two ways. CommitHead applies when the pool still shows the round's slot as unowned: the pool records the round's instance as the slot's owner, that instance adds the slot to its own set of held slots, the round leaves the journal, the tally resets and the instance returns to idle. AbortStaleHead applies when the pool instead shows the slot already owned, because the other instance won the race while this round was collecting votes: the round is discarded with no change to the pool, the tally resets and the instance returns to idle. Member banks can be slow without being failed, so a bank may sit on an out-of-date mandate generation for a while and then catch up.

The system behaves as follows. Submit appends an instruction to the tail of the queue, and requires that the submitting bank is currently accredited, that its mandate generation matches the clearing house's current generation, and that the queue is not already at capacity. SettleHead takes the instruction at the head of the queue, removes it, and advances the cleared-instruction counter, which saturates at its maximum rather than growing without bound. RotateMandate advances the clearing house's mandate generation, which instantly makes every bank that has not yet refreshed stale. Sync is the slow bank catching up: a bank whose mandate generation is behind adopts the current generation. Revoke withdraws a bank's accreditation and, in the same step, purges every instruction that bank has left waiting in the queue, so that nothing submitted by a bank that has lost its mandate can still be settled. Accredit admits a bank that is not currently accredited back into the membership without touching the queue.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the settlement queue is full, it eventually has room again.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla

A machine takes some coins out of its hopper, notes the value the central register held when it looked, and posts a deposit message carrying both the coins and the noted value. The coins are gone from the hopper the instant the message is posted -- that is what makes them the message's coins and not the hopper's. Messages sit on the operator's slow message bus and the bus reorders them freely, so by the time a message is processed the register may have moved on.

Processing a message is the compare-and-swap. If the register still holds the value the machine noted, the swap takes: the coins in the message are added to the register and the message is retired. If the register has moved on, the swap is refused: the message is retired and its coins go back to the hopper of the machine that posted it, to be tried again later. <|start|>user<|message|>A vending operator's cash is physical coin, and the audit that matters at the end of a shift is that the coin adds up. The shift starts with every coin sitting as float inside the machines' hoppers. From then on every coin in the operation is in exactly one of three places at any moment: inside a machine's hopper, in a collector's bag, or already paid into the bank. Nothing mints coin and nothing swallows it; all the actions do is move a coin from one of those places to another.

Collectors work the network under a two-level lock. The coarse level is the route -- north or south -- and a collector takes a route before touching anything on it. The fine level is the individual machine: a collector may only take a machine's lock if it already holds the lock on the route that machine belongs to, and only the holder of a machine's lock may open its hopper. Locks come off in the reverse order, so a collector cannot give a route back while it still holds a machine lock on that route.

Coin moves in both directions. A collector empties a coin out of a hopper it has open into its own bag, and pays coin out of its bag into the bank. It can also go the other way and put a coin from its bag back into a machine it has open, which is how a machine gets its change float back.

The network changes shape while the collectors work: machines are put on route and taken off route as sites open and close. A machine can only be taken off route once nobody holds its lock and its hopper is empty, so no coin is ever taken off the books by a machine leaving the network.

The full set of actions is: TakeRoute, in which a collector takes an unheld route; TakeMachine, in which a collector holding the route a machine belongs to takes that on-route machine's unheld lock; Empty, in which the holder of a machine's lock moves one coin from that machine's hopper into its own bag; Float, in which the holder of a machine's lock moves one coin from its own bag into that machine's hopper; Deposit, in which a collector pays one coin from its bag into the bank; DropMachine, in which a collector gives back a machine lock it holds; DropRoute, in which a collector gives back a route it holds, provided it holds no machine lock on that route; Commission, in which a machine is put on route; and Decommission, in which an unlocked machine with an empty hopper is taken off route.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Coin is conserved -- the coin in every machine's hopper, plus the coin in every collector's bag, plus the coin already banked, always adds up to exactly the float the machines started the shift with, no matter how the locks are taken, how the coin is moved, or how the network changes shape.

Discharging a box is irreversible: the box leaves the terminal's custody, goes onto the permanent discharge manifest, and there is no action anywhere that brings it back into the yard or takes it off the manifest. A student holding a lease that has not run down may confirm, which turns the hold into a confirmed enrolment. The registration clock may tick while at least one live lease is outstanding, running down the countdown on every outstanding hold. A student whose lease has run to zero loses the hold. The registrar may revoke any outstanding hold immediately, spending one override. The registrar may also directly enrol a student who has no hold outstanding into a course they are not in, again spending one override, and again only while that course's enrolments plus holds are strictly below its cap.     /\ hold[s] = NoCourse

    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![s] = NoCourse]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = 0]

Tick ==

    /\ overrides < MaxOverrides

    /\ UNCHANGED << hold, ttl >>

\* armed is the tasking system's register of unspent release authorities;
\* struck is the operation's strike record. The invariant ties them together.

vars == << epoch, droneEpoch, assignment, armed, struck, wind >>

    /\ droneEpoch \in [Drones -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ assignment \in [Drones -> Targets \cup {NoTarget}]

    /\ struck \in SUBSET Targets

    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ droneEpoch = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ assignment = [d \in Drones |-> NoTarget]
    /\ armed = Targets
    /\ struck = {}
    /\ wind = 0

Assign(d, t) ==
    /\ droneEpoch[d] = epoch
    /\ assignment[d] = NoTarget
    /\ t \in armed
    /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![d] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, droneEpoch, armed, struck, wind >>

\* Spending the authority and recording the strike are the same step, which is
\* what makes the release once-only.
Release(d, t) ==
    /\ assignment[d] = t
    /\ droneEpoch[d] = epoch
    /\ wind <= ReleaseLimit
    /\ t \in armed
    /\ armed' = armed \ {t}
    /\ struck' = struck \cup {t}
    /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![d] = NoTarget]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, droneEpoch, wind >>

\* The commander's override waives the epoch and the wind, but it cannot
\* conjure a release authority that has already been spent.
OverrideRelease(d, t) ==
    /\ assignment[d] = t
    /\ t \in armed
    /\ armed' = armed \ {t}
    /\ struck' = struck \cup {t}
    /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![d] = NoTarget]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, droneEpoch, wind >>

    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ assignment' = [d \in Drones |-> NoTarget]
    /\ UNCHANGED << droneEpoch, armed, struck, wind >>

Resync(d) ==
    /\ droneEpoch[d] # epoch
    /\ droneEpoch' = [droneEpoch EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, assignment, armed, struck, wind >>

Cancel(d) ==
    /\ assignment[d] # NoTarget
    /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![d] = NoTarget]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, droneEpoch, armed, struck, wind >>

Gust(w) ==
    /\ w # wind
    /\ wind' = w
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, droneEpoch, assignment, armed, struck >>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones, t \in Targets : Assign(d, t) \/ Release(d, t) \/ OverrideRelease(d, t)

The sitting dispatcher may dispatch a carrier that is standing down and not already under way to a berth, provided that berth is working fewer carriers than its limit -- a carrier under way to a berth counts against that berth exactly as one already there does, because the room has to be kept for it. The terminal may fail the chair over while it has terms left in its schedule: the term advances, the chair is emptied, and every controller's backing is cleared, so the next dispatcher must be elected afresh. \* its berth's working room, so both terms are counted against the limit.
VARIABLES term, backing, chair, atBerth, enRoute

vars == << term, backing, chair, atBerth, enRoute >>

Working(b) ==
    Cardinality({c \in Carriers : atBerth[c] = b})
      + Cardinality({c \in Carriers : enRoute[c] = b})
Backers(n) == {k \in Controllers : backing[k] = n}

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ backing \in [Controllers -> Controllers \cup {NoCtl}]
    /\ chair \in Controllers \cup {NoCtl}
    /\ atBerth \in [Carriers -> Berths \cup {NoBerth}]
    /\ enRoute \in [Carriers -> Berths \cup {NoBerth}]

    /\ chair = NoCtl

    /\ enRoute = [c \in Carriers |-> NoBerth]

\* A controller may move its backing at any time; what it cannot do is unseat

\* The chair is only taken on a strict majority of the controllers, which is
\* what stops the two installations dispatching at once.
TakeChair(n) ==

    /\ 2 * Cardinality(Backers(n)) > Cardinality(Controllers)
    /\ chair' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, atBerth, enRoute >>

    /\ enRoute[c] = NoBerth

    /\ enRoute' = [enRoute EXCEPT ![c] = NoBerth]

    /\ atBerth[c] # NoBerth
    /\ atBerth' = [atBerth EXCEPT ![c] = NoBerth]

around the ring; the exchange never mints a lot and never destroys one, so at any instant the lots
sitting on desks plus the lots still travelling must add up to the pool the session opened with.

The right to release lots travels with a baton that walks the ring one desk at a time. A desk may
release lots only while it is holding the baton, and it releases them by writing a consignment note
addressed to the next desk round the ring: the note carries a quantity, which is deducted from the
releasing desk's holdings at the moment the note is written. Notes carry a tag drawn from a small
pool, and a tag is reused only when no note bearing it is still in flight, so two notes on the wire
are always distinguishable.

the settlement system gets to them, so a note written early may be credited long after one written
later. When a note is picked off normally, its quantity is credited to the desk it was addressed to.
A note can instead be torn up, in which case the quantity goes back to the desk that released it and
the tag is recorded on the torn list. Either way the quantity leaves the wire exactly as it arrived.

The full set of actions is: PassBaton, in which the baton moves to the next desk round the ring;
Consign, in which the desk holding the baton deducts a quantity from its own holdings and puts a
freshly tagged note for the next desk onto the settlement wire; Settle, in which any note on the
wire, in any order, is credited to the desk it was addressed to and leaves the wire; and Recall, in
which any note on the wire is torn up, its quantity credited back to the desk that released it and
its tag filed on the torn list.

the settlement wire always equal the total the session opened with.

<|start|>user<|message|>A stock exchange runs its opening auction over a small set of order books, one per security. The

moves lots between books; nothing is created and nothing is destroyed, so the lots standing in the
books plus whatever is in transit must always come to the session total.

time, and only the firm on the floor may latch an order book, one book at a time. Moving lots is
done in two steps that never overlap: the firm lifts a parcel out of the book it has latched, which
takes those lots out of the book and puts them into the exchange's escrow, and the parcel is later
placed into a book, which takes it out of escrow and adds it there. Escrow holds at most one parcel
at a time, and a parcel in escrow is always eventually placed. Latches and the floor are given back
in the reverse order they were taken, the floor only once the firm holds no latch.

<|start|>user<|message|>A warehouse floor is worked by a small fleet of robots that shuttle totes between racking bays. The

nothing is lost, so the totes racked across the bays plus whatever is in motion must always come to

number and walks over empty-handed. When it gets there it tries to lift a tote, and the lift only
goes ahead if the bay's version is still the one it noted, the bay still has a tote in it, and the
single aisle is clear — the floor allows one tote in motion at a time. A successful lift takes the
tote out of the bay, rolls the bay's version on, and leaves the robot carrying. If any of those
checks fails, the robot abandons the trip and scouts again from scratch. The version number is a
small wrapping field, so it rolls back to zero at the top.

A carrying robot stows its tote into any bay that still has room, which rolls that bay's version on
as well and leaves the robot empty-handed.

The racking itself is re-profiled while the fleet is running. A bay's capacity can be raised or
lowered at any time, but never below the number of totes that bay is already holding, and never so
far that the floor as a whole could not hold every tote — so there is always somewhere to put down
whatever is in motion.

The full set of actions is: Scout, in which an empty-handed robot with no trip planned notes a bay's
version and sets off; Lift, in which a robot takes a tote out of its scouted bay because the version
still matches, the bay is not empty and the aisle is clear, rolling that bay's version on; Abandon,
in which a robot drops a planned trip because the version moved, the bay emptied or the aisle is
busy; Stow, in which a carrying robot puts its tote into a bay that has room, rolling that bay's
version on; and Reprofile, in which a bay's capacity is changed at runtime, never below what it
already holds and never so far that the floor could not hold every tote.

total.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A tote lifted off the racking is always eventually stowed back into a bay.

<|start|>user<|message|>Engineering work on a subway line is protected by possessions. Before a gang may stand on the
ballast in a track section, that section's possession register must have been swapped from clear to
that gang's name, and the swap rolls the register on to a new value which the gang keeps as its
token. The register is a small wrapping counter, so it rolls back to zero at the top of its range.

The safety case is about who is standing where. A gang may step onto a section only while it is
booked on duty, the section's register still names it, and the token it kept still reads the same as
the register. That last check is what makes a possession current rather than superseded: any gang
holding a token the register has since rolled past is speaking for a possession that no longer
exists, and must not be on the track. Handing a possession back is itself a swap and is subject to
the same check, so a gang whose token has been superseded cannot hand back a section it no longer
speaks for.

The signaller has a privileged override. A section can be taken back at any moment to run a train:
the register is rolled past whatever token is out there, the section goes clear, and anybody standing
in it is cleared off the ballast in the same movement.

Gangs also come and go from shift. Standing down takes a gang off duty and off the ballast at once,
though any possession still in its name is left standing until the signaller takes it back. A gang
that signs back on is on duty again but holds whatever token it had before.

The full set of actions is: Grant, in which a clear section's register is swapped to an on-duty
gang's name, rolled on, and the new value kept by that gang as its token; Enter, in which an on-duty
gang whose token matches the register of a section it is named on steps onto the ballast; Leave, in
which a gang steps off the ballast; HandBack, in which an on-duty gang holding a current token and
not standing in the section clears the register and rolls it on; Revoke, in which the signaller takes
a section back, rolls the register on and clears anybody out of it; StandDown, in which a gang goes
off duty and off the ballast; and SignOn, in which a gang comes back on duty.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every gang standing on the ballast is booked on duty, is named on that section's
possession register, and holds a token equal to what the register currently reads, so nobody off
duty and nobody holding a superseded possession is ever on the track.

<|start|>user<|message|>A subway line feeds traction current to its track sections from substations, and each substation can
supply only so many amps at once. Drawing more than a section's substation can feed trips the
breaker and leaves trains stranded between stations, so the allowance handed out on a section must
never add up to more than the substation can deliver.

Allowances are let on leases with an expiry rather than handed over for the day. A train is granted
an allowance on a section for a chosen number of amps and a chosen number of minutes, and the office
grants it only if the train is not already holding an allowance, the expiry falls inside the
operating day, and what is already promised on that section leaves room for it. The promise counts
against the substation from the moment it is made, not from the moment the train actually notches
up.

A train notches up onto power only against an allowance of its own that is still running, and coasts
back off power in the ordinary course of driving. When an allowance lapses it is torn up and the
train it belonged to comes off power in the same movement, so nothing is ever drawing on an expired
promise. Allowances are never held indefinitely: the register always empties out.

Substation capacity changes while the railway runs — a transformer is taken out for maintenance, a
second feeder is switched in — but a section is never rerated below what it has already promised to
the trains running on it. At the end of the operating day, once no allowances are outstanding, the
clock is reset.

The full set of actions is: Allow, in which a train holding no allowance is granted amps on a
section for a period inside the day, provided the section has room; Notch, in which a train with a
running allowance comes onto power; Coast, in which a train comes off power; Tick, in which the
clock advances a minute; Lapse, in which an expired allowance is torn up and its train comes off
power; Rerate, in which a substation's capacity is changed at runtime, never below what its section
has already promised; and NewDay, in which the clock is reset once no allowances are outstanding.

SAFETY PROPERTY: On every section, the traction allowances that are still running never add up to
more than that section's substation can feed.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Allowances are never held for ever — the allowance register always eventually
empties out.

    /\ alive \subseteq Workers

    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ hand = [w \in Workers |-> 0]
    /\ playing = 0
    /\ alive = Workers

    /\ Len(queue) < QCap
    /\ lounge' = lounge - 1
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, r)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hand, playing, alive>>

    /\ w \in alive
    /\ hand[w] = 0
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ hand' = [hand EXCEPT ![w] = 1]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lounge, playing, alive>>

Seat(w) ==
    /\ w \in alive
    /\ hand[w] = 1
    /\ hand' = [hand EXCEPT ![w] = 0]
    /\ playing' = playing + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lounge, queue, alive>>

Requeue(w, r) ==
    /\ w \in alive
    /\ hand[w] = 1
    /\ Len(queue) < QCap
    /\ hand' = [hand EXCEPT ![w] = 0]
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, r)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lounge, playing, alive>>

Finish ==
    /\ playing > 0
    /\ playing' = playing - 1
    /\ lounge' = lounge + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, hand, alive>>

\* A matchmaking worker can die without a word, still holding the player it
\* pulled; that player is neither queued nor seated until the sweep runs.
Die(w) ==

    /\ alive' = alive \ {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lounge, queue, hand, playing>>

    /\ w \notin alive
    /\ hand[w] = 1
    /\ hand' = [hand EXCEPT ![w] = 0]
    /\ lounge' = lounge + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, playing, alive>>

Respawn(w) ==
    /\ w \notin alive
    /\ hand[w] = 0
    /\ alive' = alive \cup {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lounge, queue, hand, playing>>

    \/ \E r \in Roles : Join(r)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Pull(w) \/ Seat(w) \/ Die(w) \/ Sweep(w) \/ Respawn(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers, r \in Roles : Requeue(w, r)

\* a worker's hand, or a live match -- so the four counts always add to the

reused only when nothing bearing it is still out. The van is not a queue: it does its rounds and

which the driver books off and everything still on the van is signed in to the wards; and Return, in
which a unit comes back from a ward into the cold store.

<|start|>user<|message|>A hospital pharmacy dispenses against electronic prescriptions. Each prescription carries a revision
number that rolls on every time the script is annotated or amended, and every technician carries a
policy badge that has to match the pharmacy's current policy generation. The safety case is about
who did the work and against what: nothing may be made up by a technician who has been struck off,
nor by one carrying a superseded badge, nor from a revision of the script that has since been
changed.

The bench takes no locks. A technician notes the revision the script is currently on and goes off to
make the preparation up; the script stays open to amendment the whole time. Only one preparation is
on the bench at a time. Handing the medication over is what commits it: the script is annotated,
which rolls its revision on, and the bench is cleared. A technician can also simply abandon a
preparation. Nothing is ever left half-made — a preparation on the bench is always eventually either
handed over or abandoned.

Anything that would leave the bench working from a picture that has been superseded tears the draft
up in the same movement. Amending a script tears up a draft made from it. Turning the policy
generation, which invalidates every badge at once, tears up whatever is on the bench. A technician
still on the roster can re-badge to the current generation and start again.

The pharmacist has a privileged override on individuals: a technician can be struck off mid-shift,
and whatever they had on the bench goes with them. Somebody struck off can be reinstated later, but
comes back with a zeroed badge and has to re-badge before they can work.

The full set of actions is: Prepare, in which a rostered, correctly badged technician notes a
script's revision and starts making it up on the empty bench; Dispense, in which the preparation is
handed over, the script annotated and its revision rolled on; Abandon, in which the preparation is
given up; Amend, in which a script's revision rolls on and any draft made from it is torn up;
TurnPolicy, in which the policy generation turns and the bench is cleared; Rebadge, in which a
rostered technician refreshes a stale badge; StrikeOff, in which the pharmacist removes a technician
from the roster and tears up their draft; and Reinstate, in which a struck-off technician returns
with a zeroed badge.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Anything sitting on the dispensing bench belongs to a technician still on the
roster, carrying the current policy badge, and was worked up from the revision the script is still
on.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Nothing is left half-made — every preparation on the bench is eventually either
handed over or abandoned.

<|start|>user<|message|>A regional grid sheds load by agreement between its protection relays rather than on one relay's say
so. Opening a feeder is decided by two-phase commit: a relay opens a round on a feeder that is still
closed, the relays vote, and the feeder opens once everybody eligible has voted in favour.

Eligibility is what the safety case turns on. Every relay carries a copy of the protection settings
group, and the grid publishes a running group number. A relay counts only while it is armed and its
copy matches the published group: a relay that has been disarmed is not part of the scheme at all,
and a relay still carrying a superseded settings group is reasoning from trip thresholds that have
been replaced. Neither may open a round and neither may have its vote counted.

Publishing a new settings group supersedes every relay's copy at once, so any round in flight is
torn down rather than carried across the change. A relay brings its copy up to the published group
by adopting it, and can then take part again. Feeders that have been opened are reclosed as demand
recovers.

The control room has a privileged override on both halves. A relay can be disarmed on the spot: its
vote is pulled out of the round and, if it was the relay running the round, the round is dropped
altogether. A disarmed relay can be rearmed later. The control room can also open a feeder outright,
with no round and no vote at all.

The full set of actions is: Propose, in which an armed, in-group relay opens a round on a closed
feeder and clears the tally; Aye, in which an armed, in-group relay adds its vote to the round;
Commit, in which every eligible relay having voted in favour opens the feeder and closes the round;
Abort, in which the round is dropped with nothing opened; Reclose, in which an opened feeder is
closed again; Publish, in which a new settings group is issued and any round in flight is torn down;
Adopt, in which a relay brings its copy up to the published group; Disarm, in which the control room
disarms a relay, pulling its vote and dropping any round it was running; Rearm, in which a disarmed
relay is brought back into the scheme; and ForceShed, in which the control room opens a feeder
outright.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any round in flight is being run by a relay that is armed and carrying the
published settings group, and every vote behind it comes from such a relay, so nobody disarmed and
nobody on a superseded settings group is ever part of a shedding decision.

<|start|>user<|message|>An airport baggage router shifts bags between holding bays. The terminal counts bags at the start of

control and the apron desk. Preparing a move lifts the batch out of the source bay straight away and
puts it into the router's escrow, where it sits for the length of the round — out of the source bay
and not yet in the destination. Each party then casts one vote. If both vote in favour, and the
destination is still open, the batch is committed into the destination bay and escrow is emptied. A
vote against, or the destination being frozen while the round is running, rolls the batch back into
the bay it came from. Either way the batch leaves escrow exactly as it arrived. Only one round is
in flight at a time.

against it and rolls back any round already heading for it, and thawed again later. The manager can
also carry a batch across by hand, moving it out of one bay and into another in one step with no
round and no vote at all.

escrow and a round is opened on an open destination; Aye and Nay, in which a party casts its single
vote; Commit, in which both votes in favour and an open destination put the batch into the
destination bay; Rollback, in which a vote against or a frozen destination puts the batch back where
it came from; Freeze and Thaw, in which the duty manager closes and reopens a bay; and Carry, in
which the duty manager moves a batch between bays by hand.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The bags piled across all holding bays plus the batch sitting in the router's escrow
always equal the terminal's total.

PassBaton ==

    /\ baton' = Nxt(baton)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bin, grip, belt, alive>>

    /\ r \in alive
    /\ grip[r] = 0
    /\ belt > 0
    /\ belt' = belt - 1
    /\ grip' = [grip EXCEPT ![r] = 1]

    /\ r \in alive
    /\ grip[r] = 1
    /\ grip' = [grip EXCEPT ![r] = 0]

<|start|>user<|message|>A subway line shows where its trains are on a berth display: one berth per track section, each
holding one train description. Two train describer systems drive the same display — the north
describer and the south describer, procured separately and never integrated — and they share the
one pool of berths between them.

A description that is being stepped from one berth to the next is lifted off the display into the
describer's own step queue and put back down when the step completes. Every description is therefore
in exactly one place at any instant: on a berth, or in the north describer's queue, or in the
south's. The count must always come to the number of trains the line is describing; a description
that goes missing is a train nobody can see, and one that appears twice is a phantom that will stop
a real train.

The step queues are bounded and apply backpressure, and the two are not the same depth: the north
describer has the deeper queue. A describer stops lifting descriptions off the display once its own
queue is full. At the boundary between the two systems a description is handed straight from the
head of one queue to the tail of the other, subject to the receiving queue's cap; it never touches a
berth on the way across.

Either describer can be isolated for maintenance, after which it lifts nothing new, though whatever
is already in its queue still drops back onto the display or hands across. An isolated describer is
restored when the work is done.

The full set of actions is: LiftNorth and LiftSouth, in which the describer concerned takes a
description off a berth into the tail of its own queue, while it is not isolated and its queue is
below its cap; DropNorth and DropSouth, in which the description at the head of a queue is put back
onto a berth; HandNorthToSouth and HandSouthToNorth, in which the description at the head of one
queue moves to the tail of the other, subject to that queue's cap; and Isolate and Restore, in which
a describer is taken out of service and put back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The descriptions shown on berths plus those in the north describer's queue plus
those in the south describer's queue always add up to exactly the number of trains being described.

EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Classes, NorthId, SouthId, CapNorth, CapSouth, TotalTrains

Describers == {NorthId, SouthId}

VARIABLES berths, north, south, isolated

vars == <<berths, north, south, isolated>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ berths \in 0 .. TotalTrains
    /\ Len(north) <= CapNorth
    /\ Len(south) <= CapSouth
    /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(north) : north[i] \in Classes
    /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(south) : south[i] \in Classes
    /\ isolated \subseteq Describers

Init ==
    /\ berths = TotalTrains
    /\ north = <<>>
    /\ south = <<>>
    /\ isolated = {}

\* Backpressure: a describer stops lifting descriptions once its own step
\* queue is full, and the two queues have different depths.
LiftNorth(k) ==
    /\ NorthId \notin isolated
    /\ berths > 0
    /\ Len(north) < CapNorth
    /\ berths' = berths - 1
    /\ north' = Append(north, k)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<south, isolated>>

LiftSouth(k) ==
    /\ SouthId \notin isolated
    /\ berths > 0
    /\ Len(south) < CapSouth
    /\ berths' = berths - 1
    /\ south' = Append(south, k)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<north, isolated>>

DropNorth ==
    /\ north # <<>>
    /\ berths' = berths + 1
    /\ north' = Tail(north)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<south, isolated>>

DropSouth ==
    /\ south # <<>>
    /\ berths' = berths + 1
    /\ south' = Tail(south)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<north, isolated>>

\* At the boundary a description is handed straight from one describer's queue
\* to the other's; it never touches a berth on the way.
HandNorthToSouth ==
    /\ north # <<>>
    /\ Len(south) < CapSouth
    /\ south' = Append(south, Head(north))
    /\ north' = Tail(north)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<berths, isolated>>

HandSouthToNorth ==
    /\ south # <<>>
    /\ Len(north) < CapNorth
    /\ north' = Append(north, Head(south))
    /\ south' = Tail(south)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<berths, isolated>>

Isolate(d) ==
    /\ d \notin isolated
    /\ isolated' = isolated \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<berths, north, south>>

Restore(d) ==
    /\ d \in isolated
    /\ isolated' = isolated \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<berths, north, south>>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Classes : LiftNorth(k) \/ LiftSouth(k)
    \/ DropNorth \/ DropSouth
    \/ HandNorthToSouth \/ HandSouthToNorth
    \/ \E d \in Describers : Isolate(d) \/ Restore(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every train description is in exactly one place -- on a berth or in one of
\* the two describers' step queues -- so the three counts always add up to the
\* number of trains the line is describing.
DescriptionsConserved ==
    berths + Len(north) + Len(south) = TotalTrains

<|start|>user<|message|>A stock exchange runs its opening auction with a fixed number of share lots. Lots sit either in the
pre-auction pot or resting in one of the order books, and the auction only moves them between the
two; nothing is created and nothing destroyed, so the lots resting across the books plus the lots
still in the pot must always come to the session total.

Member firms take no lock on a book. A firm reads the book's depth and its version number and works
its order up while the book stays open to everybody else. Posting the order only goes through if the
version is still the one the firm read, the book has depth left for the quantity, the pot still has
the lots, and the book's version counter has not run to the end of its range. Posting moves the lots
out of the pot and into the book in one step and rolls the book's version on. If any of those checks
fails, the order is missed and the firm works up a fresh one. One working order is on the desk at a
time and the desk never sits on it. Lots are pulled back out of a book into the pot as orders are
cancelled, which also rolls that book's version on.

Book depth is retuned while the auction runs — the exchange widens a book when interest builds and
narrows it when it thins — but never below what is already resting in it. A book whose version
counter has reached the end of its range is renumbered back to the start, with nothing on the desk,
so a stale read cannot be mistaken for a current one.

The full set of actions is: Read, in which a firm takes the current version and depth of a book and
puts a working order on the empty desk; Post, in which the order goes through because the version is
unmoved, the book has room, the pot has the lots and the version range is not exhausted, moving the
lots and rolling the version on; Miss, in which the order is dropped because one of those checks
failed; Pull, in which lots are taken back out of a book into the pot and the version rolls on;
Retune, in which a book's depth is changed at runtime, never below what is resting in it; and
Renumber, in which an exhausted version counter is reset with the desk clear.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The lots resting across all the order books plus the lots still in the pre-auction
pot always equal the session total.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The order desk never sits on a working order: every one is eventually either
posted or missed.

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Firms, Books, TotalLots, MaxDepth, MaxVer, NoDraft

VARIABLES book, ver, pot, depth, draft

vars == <<book, ver, pot, depth, draft>>

Drafts == [firm: Firms, bk: Books, saw: 0 .. MaxVer, qty: 1 .. TotalLots]

RECURSIVE Resting(_)
Resting(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN book[b] + Resting(S \ {b})

Sound(d) ==
    /\ d # NoDraft
    /\ ver[d.bk] = d.saw
    /\ ver[d.bk] < MaxVer
    /\ book[d.bk] + d.qty <= depth[d.bk]
    /\ pot >= d.qty

TypeOK ==
    /\ book \in [Books -> 0 .. TotalLots]
    /\ ver \in [Books -> 0 .. MaxVer]
    /\ pot \in 0 .. TotalLots
    /\ depth \in [Books -> 1 .. MaxDepth]
    /\ draft \in Drafts \cup {NoDraft}

Init ==
    /\ book = [b \in Books |-> 0]
    /\ ver = [b \in Books |-> 0]
    /\ pot = TotalLots
    /\ depth = [b \in Books |-> MaxDepth]
    /\ draft = NoDraft

\* No lock: the firm reads the book's depth marker and version and works its
\* order up while the book stays open to everybody else.
Read(f, b, q) ==
    /\ draft = NoDraft
    /\ draft' = [firm |-> f, bk |-> b, saw |-> ver[b], qty |-> q]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, ver, pot, depth>>

\* Lots move out of the pre-auction pot and into the book in one step, so
\* nothing is ever counted in both places or in neither.
Post ==
    /\ Sound(draft)
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![draft.bk] = @ + draft.qty]
    /\ pot' = pot - draft.qty
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![draft.bk] = @ + 1]
    /\ draft' = NoDraft
    /\ UNCHANGED depth

Miss ==
    /\ draft # NoDraft
    /\ ~Sound(draft)
    /\ draft' = NoDraft
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, ver, pot, depth>>

Pull(b, q) ==
    /\ q <= book[b]
    /\ ver[b] < MaxVer
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![b] = @ - q]
    /\ pot' = pot + q
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<depth, draft>>

\* The exchange retunes book depth between rounds while the auction runs,
\* never below what is already resting.
Retune(b, n) ==
    /\ n >= book[b]
    /\ depth' = [depth EXCEPT ![b] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, ver, pot, draft>>

Renumber(b) ==
    /\ ver[b] = MaxVer
    /\ draft = NoDraft
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, pot, depth, draft>>

Settling == Post \/ Miss

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Firms, b \in Books, q \in 1 .. TotalLots : Read(f, b, q)
    \/ Settling
    \/ \E b \in Books, q \in 1 .. TotalLots : Pull(b, q)
    \/ \E b \in Books, n \in 1 .. MaxDepth : Retune(b, n)
    \/ \E b \in Books : Renumber(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Settling)

\* Lots only ever move between the pre-auction pot and an order book, so the
\* lots resting across the books plus those still in the pot always come to
\* the session total.
LotsConserved == Resting(Books) + pot = TotalLots

\* The order desk never sits on a working order.
DraftsSettle == (draft # NoDraft) ~> (draft = NoDraft)

====

<|start|>user<|message|>An airport baggage router keeps a single routing record that says which chute each flight's bags
go down. Ground handlers edit that record without taking it out of service: a handler first reads
the record and remembers the version stamp it saw, then later submits its recomputed routing. The
submission is accepted only if the version stamp it read is still the current one, so a handler
whose reading has gone stale must throw its work away and start over. Only handlers on the day's
security clearance list may submit at all; uncleared staff may read and recompute but their
submissions are never accepted.

During a diversion the record is put into recall mode. While recall mode is on, ordinary handler
submissions are refused outright, but the duty supervisor holds a privileged override and may push
a routing directly onto the record even though recall mode is on. Every accepted submission is
appended to the record's edit log together with the identity of whoever submitted it and the
version stamp that submission was computed from.

The full set of actions is: a handler takes a reading of the current version stamp; a cleared
handler submits a recomputed routing while recall mode is off and its reading is still current; a
handler whose reading has gone stale discards it and retries, up to a bounded number of retries;
the duty supervisor pushes a routing under the privileged override while recall mode is on; the
router enters recall mode; and the router leaves recall mode.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every entry in the edit log was submitted either by the duty supervisor or by a
handler on the clearance list, and was computed from exactly the version stamp that immediately
preceded it, so no stale or uncleared submission ever lands on the routing record.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od17m0p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Handlers, Cleared, Supervisor, NoReading, MaxRetry, MaxEdits

ASSUME Cleared \subseteq Handlers
ASSUME Supervisor \notin Handlers

Submitters == Handlers \cup {Supervisor}

VARIABLES editLog, reading, recall, retries

vars == <<editLog, reading, recall, retries>>

\* The version stamp of the routing record is just how many edits have landed.
Stamp == Len(editLog)

Entry == [by: Submitters, saw: 0..MaxEdits]

TypeOK ==
    /\ editLog \in Seq(Entry)
    /\ reading \in [Handlers -> (0..MaxEdits) \cup {NoReading}]
    /\ recall \in BOOLEAN
    /\ retries \in [Handlers -> 0..MaxRetry]

Init ==
    /\ editLog = << >>
    /\ reading = [h \in Handlers |-> NoReading]
    /\ recall = FALSE
    /\ retries = [h \in Handlers |-> 0]

\* A handler with no reading in hand takes one; uncleared staff may read too.
TakeReading(h) ==
    /\ reading[h] = NoReading
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![h] = Stamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<editLog, recall, retries>>

\* Accepted only when the reading is still current, the submitter is cleared,
\* and the record is not in recall mode.
Submit(h) ==
    /\ ~recall
    /\ h \in Cleared
    /\ reading[h] = Stamp
    /\ editLog' = Append(editLog, [by |-> h, saw |-> reading[h]])
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![h] = NoReading]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<recall, retries>>

\* A reading that has gone stale is thrown away and the work is redone.
Retry(h) ==
    /\ reading[h] # NoReading
    /\ reading[h] # Stamp
    /\ retries[h] < MaxRetry
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![h] = NoReading]
    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![h] = retries[h] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<editLog, recall>>

\* The privileged override: the supervisor may push during recall mode.
Override ==
    /\ recall
    /\ editLog' = Append(editLog, [by |-> Supervisor, saw |-> Stamp])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reading, recall, retries>>

EnterRecall ==
    /\ ~recall
    /\ recall' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<editLog, reading, retries>>

LeaveRecall ==
    /\ recall
    /\ recall' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<editLog, reading, retries>>

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Handlers : TakeReading(h) \/ Submit(h) \/ Retry(h)
    \/ Override \/ EnterRecall \/ LeaveRecall

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Bounded == Len(editLog) <= MaxEdits

\* Nothing lands unless it is both authorised and computed from the newest stamp.
NoStaleOrUnclearedEdit ==
    \A i \in DOMAIN editLog :
        /\ editLog[i].by \in Cleared \cup {Supervisor}
        /\ editLog[i].saw = i - 1

====

<|start|>user<|message|>A regional power grid runs a load shedder. The region carries a fixed number of megawatts of
customer demand, and every megawatt is at all times in exactly one of three places: energised on
one of the feeders, parked in the shed pool waiting to be brought back, or riding on a dispatch
order that has left the control room but has not yet been applied at the receiving feeder.

Dispatch orders travel over the grid's telemetry bus, which does not preserve order: several orders
can be outstanding at once and they may be applied in any sequence, not necessarily the sequence
they were issued in. An order names one receiving feeder and a block of megawatts. The block is
taken off its source the moment the order is issued and only appears on the receiving feeder when
the order is applied, so it is never counted in two places and never disappears in between.

Shedding and dispatching are directed by the control room's coordinator, which is one of the
feeders acting in that role. The coordinator can drop out at any moment, leaving the region with no
coordinator; any feeder can then take the role over. While there is no coordinator, no load is shed
and no dispatch order is issued, though orders already on the bus can still be applied.

The full set of actions is: a feeder takes over as coordinator when there is none; the sitting
coordinator drops out; under a coordinator, a block is shed off a feeder into the shed pool; under
a coordinator, a block is taken out of the shed pool and issued as a dispatch order onto a free
slot on the bus; an outstanding order is applied, adding its block to the receiving feeder and
freeing its slot; and a block is moved directly off one feeder onto the bus as an order addressed
to another feeder.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The megawatts energised across all feeders, plus those parked in the shed pool,
plus those riding on outstanding dispatch orders, always add up to exactly the region's fixed
demand.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the region is left without a coordinator, some feeder eventually takes
the role over.

---- MODULE W4Od9m3p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Feeders, Slots, Demand, MaxBlock, Home, NoLeader, Free

ASSUME Home \in Feeders
ASSUME NoLeader \notin Feeders

Order == [dest : Feeders, block : 1..MaxBlock]

VARIABLES energised, pool, bus, coordinator

vars == <<energised, pool, bus, coordinator>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ energised \in [Feeders -> 0..Demand]
    /\ pool \in 0..Demand
    /\ bus \in [Slots -> Order \cup {Free}]
    /\ coordinator \in Feeders \cup {NoLeader}

RECURSIVE OnFeeders(_)
OnFeeders(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET f == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN energised[f] + OnFeeders(S \ {f})

RECURSIVE OnBus(_)
OnBus(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET s == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN
         (IF bus[s] = Free THEN 0 ELSE bus[s].block) + OnBus(S \ {s})

Init ==
    /\ energised = [f \in Feeders |-> IF f = Home THEN Demand ELSE 0]
    /\ pool = 0
    /\ bus = [s \in Slots |-> Free]
    /\ coordinator = NoLeader

TakeOver(f) ==
    /\ coordinator = NoLeader
    /\ coordinator' = f
    /\ UNCHANGED <<energised, pool, bus>>

DropOut ==
    /\ coordinator # NoLeader
    /\ coordinator' = NoLeader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<energised, pool, bus>>

\* Shedding moves a block off a feeder and parks it; nothing is destroyed.
Shed(f, k) ==
    /\ coordinator # NoLeader
    /\ energised[f] >= k
    /\ energised' = [energised EXCEPT ![f] = @ - k]
    /\ pool' = pool + k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bus, coordinator>>

\* Issuing debits the source immediately; the block now rides on the bus.
Issue(f, k, s) ==
    /\ coordinator # NoLeader
    /\ pool >= k
    /\ bus[s] = Free
    /\ pool' = pool - k
    /\ bus' = [bus EXCEPT ![s] = [dest |-> f, block |-> k]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<energised, coordinator>>

\* Any outstanding order may be applied; the bus does not preserve order.
Apply(s) ==
    /\ bus[s] # Free
    /\ energised' = [energised EXCEPT ![bus[s].dest] = @ + bus[s].block]
    /\ bus' = [bus EXCEPT ![s] = Free]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, coordinator>>

Move(f, g, k, s) ==
    /\ coordinator # NoLeader
    /\ f # g
    /\ energised[f] >= k
    /\ bus[s] = Free
    /\ energised' = [energised EXCEPT ![f] = @ - k]
    /\ bus' = [bus EXCEPT ![s] = [dest |-> g, block |-> k]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, coordinator>>

TakeOverSome == \E f \in Feeders : TakeOver(f)

Next ==
    \/ TakeOverSome \/ DropOut
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Apply(s)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders, k \in 1..MaxBlock : Shed(f, k)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders, k \in 1..MaxBlock, s \in Slots : Issue(f, k, s)
    \/ \E f, g \in Feeders : \E k \in 1..MaxBlock, s \in Slots : Move(f, g, k, s)

Spec ==

It commits by writing the source fridge's count back as its snapshot count minus one and adding one to whatever the destination fridge holds at that moment -- so the source side of the write is an absolute value computed from the old snapshot, not a decrement applied to the current value. The commit is only allowed if the version number is still the one the instance read.

If the version has moved on, the instance's snapshot is out of date. With retry budget left it burns one retry and puts the move back in the batch for another attempt; with the budget exhausted it abandons the move for the shift. A requested move whose source fridge is empty is cancelled outright. Separately, either instance may write off one unit from any non-empty fridge as expired, which bumps the version and moves that unit into the written-off tally.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The shift's transfer batch is eventually settled -- the batch empties and neither tracker instance is left holding a half-finished transfer.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla

<|start|>user<|message|>A clearing house settles a batch across two participant banks using a two-phase commit. Phase one is the vote. While no decision has been reached, a participant that has not yet voted either earmarks the leg amount out of its own balance and votes yes, or -- if its balance will not cover the leg -- votes no without moving anything. Once every participant has voted, the coordinator decides: commit if every vote was yes, abort otherwise. Deciding also puts one decision notice for each participant onto the network, stamped with the round the decision belongs to and naming the leg amount.

Phase two is the apply. The network does not preserve order and the coordinator may re-issue a decision notice to any participant at any time while a decision stands, so a participant's inbox can hold notices it has already acted on and notices belonging to a round that has since been closed. A participant applies a commit notice by moving its earmarked leg into the batch total; it applies an abort notice by returning its earmarked leg to its own balance. Either way the participant is then marked as having applied. A participant may only act on a notice if it currently has a leg earmarked and if the notice's round stamp is the round now open; notices whose round stamp is stale may be discarded unread.

    /\ vote[m.to] = "yes"
