CONSTANTS Sessions, Schedulers, Members, Quorum, DayTotal, MaxAsk,
          MaxRound, NoSession, NoBallot

VARIABLES pool, booked, used, round, bid, ballot

Vars == <<pool, booked, used, round, bid, ballot>>

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

NoBid == [rnd |-> 0, sess |-> NoSession, mins |-> 0, poolRead |-> 0]

\* Ballots are counted per bid and per round, because a slot can still hold a
\* ballot cast in a round that has since closed.
Backing(s) ==
    Cardinality({m \in Members : ballot[m] # NoBallot
                                 /\ ballot[m].sch = s
                                 /\ ballot[m].rnd = round})

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in 0..(2 * DayTotal) /\ used \in 0..DayTotal
    /\ booked \in [Sessions -> 0..DayTotal] /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
    /\ bid \in [Schedulers -> [rnd: 0..MaxRound,
                sess: {NoSession} \union Sessions, mins: 0..MaxAsk,
                poolRead: 0..(2 * DayTotal)]]
    /\ ballot \in [Members -> {NoBallot} \union [sch: Schedulers,
                                                rnd: 0..MaxRound]]

Init ==
    /\ pool = DayTotal /\ used = 0
    /\ booked = [s \in Sessions |-> 0] /\ round = 0
    /\ bid = [s \in Schedulers |-> NoBid]
    /\ ballot = [m \in Members |-> NoBallot]

PutBid(s, t, n) ==
    /\ bid[s].sess = NoSession /\ n <= pool
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![s] = [rnd |-> round, sess |-> t, mins |-> n,
                                  poolRead |-> pool]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, booked, used, round, ballot>>

CastBallot(m, s) ==
    /\ ballot[m] = NoBallot /\ bid[s].sess # NoSession
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![m] = [sch |-> s, rnd |-> bid[s].rnd]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, booked, used, round, bid>>

\* The pool is written back from the reading on the bid, so the round test is
\* what keeps that reading true.
Enact(s) ==
    /\ bid[s].sess # NoSession /\ bid[s].rnd = round
    /\ Backing(s) >= Quorum /\ bid[s].mins <= bid[s].poolRead
    /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![bid[s].sess] = @ + bid[s].mins]
    /\ pool' = bid[s].poolRead - bid[s].mins
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![s] = NoBid]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<used, ballot>>

Withdraw(s) ==
    /\ bid[s].sess # NoSession /\ bid[s].rnd # round
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![s] = NoBid]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, booked, used, round, ballot>>

ClearBallot(m) ==
    /\ ballot[m] # NoBallot /\ ballot[m].rnd # round
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![m] = NoBallot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, booked, used, round, bid>>

UseMinute(t) ==
    /\ booked[t] > 0 /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![t] = @ - 1]
    /\ used' = used + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, round, bid, ballot>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Schedulers, t \in Sessions, n \in 1..MaxAsk : PutBid(s, t, n)
    \/ \E m \in Members, s \in Schedulers : CastBallot(m, s)
    \/ \E s \in Schedulers : Enact(s) \/ Withdraw(s)
    \/ \E m \in Members : ClearBallot(m)
    \/ \E t \in Sessions : UseMinute(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Conservation: pool plus bookings plus used minutes is always exactly the
\* day's total, so no enactment mints or loses a theatre minute.
MinutesConserved == pool + Tally(booked, Sessions) + used = DayTotal
====

<|start|>user<|message|>A car wash recycles its water. Every litre in the system is accounted for: it is sitting in the reclaim tank, charged into one of the bays' spray lines, or already discharged to the drain. Litres are never created and never lost.

Charging the bays is done as a two-phase commit, because a bay charged while another bay is not ready sprays into an empty stall. In the voting phase the plant opens a round and each in-service bay with an empty spray line may vote itself ready. The round is committed only when every in-service bay has voted ready and the reclaim tank holds enough water to charge them all: committing fills the spray line of every bay in the ready set to its full draw in one write, takes that many litres out of the tank, and closes the round. A round may also simply be aborted, which closes it without charging anything.

Opening a round clears the ready set first. That matters because aborting a round leaves the ready set as it was, so without the clear a bay could still be counted ready in a later round when its line is no longer empty -- and the commit fills lines to their full draw as an absolute write rather than topping them up, so a bay counted ready with water already in it would have that water written over.

Water leaves a bay in one of two ways: a bay with water in its line may return one litre to the reclaim tank, or may discharge one litre to the drain.

Capacity changes while the plant is running: the set of in-service bays is republished between rounds as bays are opened and closed for maintenance. The new set may not be empty, and it may only be republished while no round is open.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The water in the reclaim tank, plus the water charged into the bays' spray lines, plus the water already discharged to the drain always adds up to exactly the volume the system holds.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od4m2p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bays, Volume, Draw

VARIABLES tank, charged, drained, ready, voting, inService

Vars == <<tank, charged, drained, ready, voting, inService>>

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ tank \in 0..(2 * Volume) /\ drained \in 0..Volume
    /\ charged \in [Bays -> 0..Draw]
    /\ ready \subseteq Bays /\ voting \in BOOLEAN
    /\ inService \subseteq Bays

Init ==
    /\ tank = Volume /\ drained = 0
    /\ charged = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ ready = {} /\ voting = FALSE /\ inService = Bays

\* Opening a round clears the ready set, because an aborted round leaves the
\* old votes standing and the commit writes lines absolutely.
OpenRound ==
    /\ ~voting /\ inService # {}
    /\ voting' = TRUE /\ ready' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tank, charged, drained, inService>>

VoteReady(b) ==
    /\ voting /\ b \in inService /\ b \notin ready /\ charged[b] = 0
    /\ ready' = ready \union {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tank, charged, drained, voting, inService>>

\* One write fills every ready bay's line to its full draw.
Commit ==
    /\ voting /\ ready = inService
    /\ tank >= Draw * Cardinality(ready)
    /\ charged' = [b \in Bays |-> IF b \in ready THEN Draw ELSE charged[b]]
    /\ tank' = tank - Draw * Cardinality(ready)
    /\ voting' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<drained, ready, inService>>

Abort ==
    /\ voting /\ voting' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tank, charged, drained, ready, inService>>

Reclaim(b) ==
    /\ charged[b] > 0
    /\ charged' = [charged EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1] /\ tank' = tank + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<drained, ready, voting, inService>>

Discharge(b) ==
    /\ charged[b] > 0
    /\ charged' = [charged EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1] /\ drained' = drained + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tank, ready, voting, inService>>

\* Capacity changes between rounds, never inside one.
Republish(bs) ==
    /\ ~voting /\ bs # {} /\ inService' = bs
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tank, charged, drained, ready, voting>>

Next ==
    \/ OpenRound \/ Commit \/ Abort
    \/ \E b \in Bays : VoteReady(b) \/ Reclaim(b) \/ Discharge(b)
    \/ \E bs \in SUBSET Bays : Republish(bs)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Conservation: tank plus charged lines plus drained is always exactly the
\* volume the plant holds, so no commit writes over water already in a line.
WaterConserved == tank + Tally(charged, Bays) + drained = Volume
====

<|start|>user<|message|>A blood bank tracks every unit it holds. A unit is in one of the fridges, on a porter's trolley, already transfused, or in the quarantine tally. Those four together must always account for exactly the stock the bank opened with: units are never conjured up and, more importantly, never allowed to quietly disappear.

Only one porter at a time may work the master ledger, and the right to do so is a lease with a fixed number of ticks left on it. The lease names its holder and its remaining ticks; a tick of the bank's clock takes one off. A lease with no ticks left has expired.

Any running porter may take the lease when it is unheld or when the current lease has expired. Taking it is also a hand-over of the ledger, and the hand-over has to deal with whatever the outgoing porter was carrying: the outgoing porter's trolley is emptied and everything that was on it goes into the quarantine tally, because units that were in a porter's hands when the ledger changed hands cannot be trusted back into a fridge but must still be accounted for. The new lease then starts with a full complement of ticks.

A running porter holding a lease with ticks left may take one unit out of a fridge onto its trolley if the trolley has room, may put one unit from its trolley back into a fridge, or may transfuse one unit off its trolley, which moves it into the transfused tally.

Any porter can crash silently. A crashed porter stops doing anything at all: it keeps whatever is on its trolley, it keeps the lease if it held one, and nothing is announced. The only thing that recovers the situation is the lease running out of ticks and somebody else taking it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The units in the fridges, plus the units on the porters' trolleys, plus the units transfused, plus the units in quarantine always add up to exactly the stock the bank opened with.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od12m6p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Fridges, Porters, Stock, TrolleyCap, Span, NoPorter

VARIABLES fridge, trolley, transfused, quarantined, lease, crashed

Vars == <<fridge, trolley, transfused, quarantined, lease, crashed>>

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

Running(p) == p \notin crashed

Working(p) == lease.holder = p /\ lease.ticks > 0

TypeOK ==
    /\ fridge \in [Fridges -> 0..Stock] /\ transfused \in 0..Stock
    /\ trolley \in [Porters -> 0..TrolleyCap] /\ quarantined \in 0..Stock
    /\ lease \in [holder: {NoPorter} \union Porters, ticks: 0..Span]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Porters

Init ==
    /\ fridge = [f \in Fridges |-> IF f = CHOOSE g \in Fridges : TRUE
                                   THEN Stock ELSE 0]
    /\ trolley = [p \in Porters |-> 0]
    /\ transfused = 0 /\ quarantined = 0
    /\ lease = [holder |-> NoPorter, ticks |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = {}

Tick ==
    /\ lease.ticks > 0
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT !.ticks = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, trolley, transfused, quarantined, crashed>>

\* The hand-over has to account for whatever the outgoing porter was carrying:
\* those units cannot go back to a fridge, but they cannot vanish either.
TakeLease(p) ==
    /\ Running(p) /\ (lease.holder = NoPorter \/ lease.ticks = 0)
    /\ trolley' = IF lease.holder = NoPorter THEN trolley
                  ELSE [trolley EXCEPT ![lease.holder] = 0]
    /\ quarantined' = IF lease.holder = NoPorter THEN quarantined
                      ELSE quarantined + trolley[lease.holder]
    /\ lease' = [holder |-> p, ticks |-> Span]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, transfused, crashed>>

Collect(p, f) ==
    /\ Running(p) /\ Working(p)
    /\ fridge[f] > 0 /\ trolley[p] < TrolleyCap
    /\ fridge' = [fridge EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1]
    /\ trolley' = [trolley EXCEPT ![p] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<transfused, quarantined, lease, crashed>>

Shelve(p, f) ==
    /\ Running(p) /\ Working(p) /\ trolley[p] > 0
    /\ trolley' = [trolley EXCEPT ![p] = @ - 1]
    /\ fridge' = [fridge EXCEPT ![f] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<transfused, quarantined, lease, crashed>>

Transfuse(p) ==
    /\ Running(p) /\ Working(p) /\ trolley[p] > 0
    /\ trolley' = [trolley EXCEPT ![p] = @ - 1]
    /\ transfused' = transfused + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, quarantined, lease, crashed>>

\* Silent: the trolley stays loaded, the lease stays held, nothing is said.
Crash(p) ==
    /\ Running(p) /\ crashed' = crashed \union {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, trolley, transfused, quarantined, lease>>

Next ==
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E p \in Porters : TakeLease(p) \/ Transfuse(p) \/ Crash(p)
    \/ \E p \in Porters, f \in Fridges : Collect(p, f) \/ Shelve(p, f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Conservation: fridges plus trolleys plus transfused plus quarantined is
\* always exactly the opening stock, so a hand-over never loses a unit.
StockFullyAccounted ==
    Tally(fridge, Fridges) + Tally(trolley, Porters)
        + transfused + quarantined = Stock
====

<|start|>user<|message|>An airport's runway allocator hands out landing slots for the hour. Every slot in the hour's capacity is accounted for: it is unassigned in the free pool, assigned to a particular flight, or already used. Slots are never invented and never lost.

Capacity changes while the hour is running, because runways go in and out of use for weather and works. The capacity figure is republished by a reconfiguration, which carries an epoch number: republishing sets a new capacity, moves the difference into or out of the free pool so that the books still balance, and advances the epoch. Two conditions apply to a republish: the new capacity must be at least one slot, and it must leave at least one slot unassigned in the free pool, so the allocator never reconfigures itself into having nothing to hand out.

Two allocator processes share the slot book, but the book allows only one draft at a time: an allocator may start a draft only when no draft at all is outstanding. Starting a draft names a flight, records the epoch in force, and records the free-pool figure the allocator read at that moment, and requires the pool to be non-empty.

Assigning the draft is only allowed if the epoch recorded on it is still the epoch in force. Assigning adds one slot to the flight's assignment and writes the free pool back as the figure recorded on the draft minus one -- an absolute value derived from the old reading, not a decrement of the pool as it now stands. That is why the epoch test matters: a republish between the reading and the assignment has already moved the pool.

A draft whose epoch has been superseded is discarded. And any flight with a slot assigned to it may use that slot, which moves it into the used tally.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The slots in the free pool, plus the slots assigned to flights, plus the slots already used always add up to exactly the capacity currently published for the hour.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A landing slot is eventually used -- some flight eventually lands.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od1m9p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Flights, Allocators, MaxCap, MaxEpoch, NoFlight

VARIABLES pool, assigned, used, epoch, capacity, draft

Vars == <<pool, assigned, used, epoch, capacity, draft>>

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

Blank == [flt |-> NoFlight, ep |-> 0, poolRead |-> 0]

Quiet == \A a \in Allocators : draft[a].flt = NoFlight

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in 0..(2 * MaxCap) /\ used \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ assigned \in [Flights -> 0..MaxCap]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ draft \in [Allocators -> [flt: {NoFlight} \union Flights,
                  ep: 0..MaxEpoch, poolRead: 0..(2 * MaxCap)]]

Init ==
    /\ pool = MaxCap /\ used = 0
    /\ assigned = [f \in Flights |-> 0]
    /\ epoch = 0 /\ capacity = MaxCap
    /\ draft = [a \in Allocators |-> Blank]

\* Republishing moves the difference into or out of the free pool so the books
\* balance, and never leaves the allocator with nothing to hand out.
Republish(c) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch /\ c >= 1
    /\ pool + c - capacity >= 1
    /\ capacity' = c /\ pool' = pool + c - capacity
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, used, draft>>

\* The book allows one draft at a time.
StartDraft(a, f) ==
    /\ Quiet /\ pool > 0
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![a] = [flt |-> f, ep |-> epoch,
                                      poolRead |-> pool]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, assigned, used, epoch, capacity>>

\* The pool is written back from the old reading, so the epoch test is what
\* keeps that reading true across a republish.
Assign(a) ==
    /\ draft[a].flt # NoFlight /\ draft[a].ep = epoch
    /\ draft[a].poolRead > 0
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![draft[a].flt] = @ + 1]
    /\ pool' = draft[a].poolRead - 1
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![a] = Blank]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<used, epoch, capacity>>

Discard(a) ==
    /\ draft[a].flt # NoFlight /\ draft[a].ep # epoch
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![a] = Blank]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, assigned, used, epoch, capacity>>

UseSlot(f) ==
    /\ assigned[f] > 0
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1] /\ used' = used + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, epoch, capacity, draft>>

AllocStep ==
    \/ \E a \in Allocators, f \in Flights : StartDraft(a, f)
    \/ \E a \in Allocators : Assign(a) \/ Discard(a)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : UseSlot(f)

Next == AllocStep \/ (\E c \in 1..MaxCap : Republish(c))

\* Republishing is bounded by the epoch budget, so weak fairness on the
\* allocation steps carries a slot through once capacity settles.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars /\ WF_Vars(AllocStep)

\* Conservation: free pool plus assignments plus used slots is always exactly
\* the capacity published for the hour.
SlotsConserved == pool + Tally(assigned, Flights) + used = capacity

\* Progress: a slot really does get used.
SomeSlotUsed == <>(used > 0)
====

<|start|>user<|message|>A hospital pharmacy accounts for every controlled ampoule it holds. An ampoule is in the safe, in a technician's hands, or already administered to a patient. The three together must always add up to exactly the stock the pharmacy opened with: ampoules are never conjured up and never lost.

Nothing leaves the safe on one person's authority. A withdrawal is put as a motion, and the motion needs a quorum of technician ballots. The pharmacy keeps a round number, and every write to the safe advances it, because a ballot cast about the safe as it was is not a ballot about the safe as it is.

Opening a motion, which is only possible when no motion is on the table, names the technician who will take the ampoules, how many, the round in force, and the number of ampoules the mover counted in the safe at that moment. Any technician may cast a ballot for the motion on the table; each technician has one ballot slot, stamped with the round it voted in.

Executing the motion requires that the round recorded on the motion is still the round in force and that the ballots stamped with that round reach quorum. Executing moves the ampoules into the named technician's hands and writes the safe count back as the figure the mover counted minus the quantity taken -- an absolute value derived from that old count, not a subtraction from the safe as it now stands. Executing does not advance the round, because it closes the motion as it goes and there is nothing left to invalidate.

Technicians are slow but they do not fail. A motion can sit on the table for a long time, and a technician may in the meantime return ampoules from its hands to the safe, which advances the round. That leaves the motion on the table recorded against a round that has closed; such a motion is abandoned.

A technician with ampoules in hand may administer one, which moves it into the administered tally.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The ampoules in the safe, plus the ampoules in the technicians' hands, plus the ampoules already administered always add up to exactly the stock the pharmacy opened with.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: An ampoule is eventually administered.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od16m5p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Techs, Stock, HandCap, Quorum, MaxRound, NoTech, NoBallot

VARIABLES safe, held, given, round, motion, ballot

Vars == <<safe, held, given, round, motion, ballot>>

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

NoMotion == [tech |-> NoTech, qty |-> 0, safeRead |-> 0, rnd |-> 0]

Backing == Cardinality({v \in Techs : ballot[v] = round})

TypeOK ==
    /\ safe \in 0..(2 * Stock) /\ given \in 0..Stock
    /\ held \in [Techs -> 0..HandCap] /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
    /\ motion \in [tech: {NoTech} \union Techs, qty: 0..HandCap,
                   safeRead: 0..(2 * Stock), rnd: 0..MaxRound]
    /\ ballot \in [Techs -> {NoBallot} \union (0..MaxRound)]

Init ==
    /\ safe = Stock /\ given = 0
    /\ held = [t \in Techs |-> 0] /\ round = 0
    /\ motion = NoMotion
    /\ ballot = [t \in Techs |-> NoBallot]

OpenMotion(t, n) ==
    /\ motion.tech = NoTech /\ n <= safe /\ held[t] + n <= HandCap
    /\ motion' = [tech |-> t, qty |-> n, safeRead |-> safe, rnd |-> round]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<safe, held, given, round, ballot>>

CastBallot(v) ==
    /\ motion.tech # NoTech /\ ballot[v] # round
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![v] = round]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<safe, held, given, round, motion>>

\* The safe is written back from the mover's old count, so the round test is
\* what keeps that count true.  Executing closes the motion, so it has nothing
\* left to invalidate and does not advance the round.
Execute ==
    /\ motion.tech # NoTech /\ motion.rnd = round
    /\ Backing >= Quorum /\ motion.qty <= motion.safeRead
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![motion.tech] = @ + motion.qty]
    /\ safe' = motion.safeRead - motion.qty
    /\ motion' = NoMotion
    /\ UNCHANGED <<given, round, ballot>>

Abandon ==
    /\ motion.tech # NoTech /\ motion.rnd # round
    /\ motion' = NoMotion
    /\ UNCHANGED <<safe, held, given, round, ballot>>

\* Returning ampoules is a write to the safe, so it advances the round and
\* leaves any motion on the table recorded against a closed round.
Return(t, n) ==
    /\ held[t] >= n /\ n >= 1 /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![t] = @ - n] /\ safe' = safe + n
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<given, motion, ballot>>

Administer(t) ==
    /\ held[t] > 0
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![t] = @ - 1] /\ given' = given + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<safe, round, motion, ballot>>

BallotStep == \E v \in Techs : CastBallot(v)

WardStep ==
    \/ BallotStep \/ Execute \/ Abandon
    \/ \E t \in Techs, n \in 1..HandCap : OpenMotion(t, n)
    \/ \E t \in Techs : Administer(t)

Next == WardStep \/ (\E t \in Techs, n \in 1..HandCap : Return(t, n))

\* Returns advance the round and strand motions, so balloting and executing
\* need strong fairness to get a foot in that churn.
Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(WardStep) /\ SF_Vars(BallotStep) /\ SF_Vars(Execute)

\* Conservation: safe plus hands plus administered is always exactly the
\* opening stock, so no execution mints or loses an ampoule.
AmpoulesConserved == safe + Tally(held, Techs) + given = Stock

\* Progress: an ampoule really does reach a patient.
SomethingAdministered == <>(given > 0)
====

<|start|>user<|message|>A pharmacy dispenser holds made-up prescriptions in numbered collection bins. The robot arms that load the bins work under a lease on the allocation map. The lease names one arm and carries a countdown of ticks; a tick of the cabinet clock takes one off, and a lease with no ticks left has expired. A running arm may take the lease when it is unheld or expired. Taking the lease voids every pending allocation any arm was holding, because a pending allocation names a bin that the arm chose while it held the map and that choice is no longer safe once the map has changed hands.

A running arm holding a live lease, with nothing pending, may plan an allocation: it names a prescription that does not yet hold a bin and a bin currently on the free list. Planning writes nothing to the map.

Committing requires a live lease and that the prescription still holds no bin: the prescription is recorded against the planned bin and that bin is struck off the free list. Note that committing does not re-check the free list -- the lease, and the voiding of pending allocations when it changes hands, are what make the planned bin still free.

A patient may collect any prescription that has been allocated a bin and not yet collected, which marks it collected, clears the allocation and puts the bin back on the free list.

Any arm can crash silently: it stops doing anything at all, keeping the lease if it held one and keeping whatever it had pending, with nothing announced.

A feeder energises an unplaced block whenever doing so keeps it inside its standing quota. A block that would take the feeder past its quota is curtailed instead -- curtailment moves the block out of the unplaced pile and into the curtailed pile, so the block is still carried, not discarded. When a newer plan raises a feeder's quota, the feeder picks curtailed blocks back up one at a time and energises them. Feeders here are slow but never fail: a feeder can lag a long way behind the plan the control room has published, and blocks can sit unplaced or curtailed for an arbitrarily long time, but no feeder ever stops responding altogether. Once every feeder has placed all its blocks and is drawing at least its quota, the grid is steady.

    /\ rev \in 0..MaxRev
    /\ tries \in [Flights -> 0..MaxTry]

    /\ clearance = [f \in Flights |-> [state |-> "pending", base |-> 0]]
    /\ tape = {}
    /\ rev = 0
    /\ tries = [f \in Flights |-> 0]

\* A controller reads the sequence board and the revision stamped on it, then
\* works the clearance up.  Controllers here are slow but never fail: that can
\* take arbitrarily long, and the board may move on underneath them.
Read(f) ==
    /\ clearance[f].state = "pending"
    /\ tries[f] < MaxTry
    /\ clearance' = [clearance EXCEPT ![f] = [state |-> "reading", base |-> rev]]
    /\ tries' = [tries EXCEPT ![f] = tries[f] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tape, rev>>

\* Transmitting the clearance is irreversible: it goes out over the air and
\* onto the recorded tape, where it cannot be taken back.  It therefore only
\* goes out while the revision the controller read is still the board's, which
\* is what stops a second transmission being worked up against a stale read.
Transmit(f) ==
    /\ clearance[f].state = "reading"
    /\ clearance[f].base = rev
    /\ rev < MaxRev

    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ clearance' = [clearance EXCEPT ![f].state = "issued"]

Retry(f) ==

Shelve(f) ==

    /\ \/ tries[f] = MaxTry

    /\ clearance' = [clearance EXCEPT ![f].state = "shelved"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tape, rev, tries>>

    /\ \A f \in Flights : clearance[f].state \in {"issued", "shelved"}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Read(f) \/ Transmit(f) \/ Retry(f) \/ Shelve(f)
    \/ Quiet

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A flight that has been cleared appears exactly once on the recorded tape,
\* however many times its strip was worked up and torn out again.
ClearanceTransmittedOnce ==

            (Cardinality({x \in tape : x.flt = f}) = 1)

<|start|>user<|message|>An air-traffic centre holds a flight plan per sector, and control desks amend those plans as traffic develops. A desk may only write into a sector's plan while it holds a lease on that sector, and leases run out on the clock rather than being held until the desk gives them up, so a desk that goes quiet cannot hold a sector for the rest of the watch.

Amendments travel over the sector datalink, which reorders freely: amendments raised in one order can reach the plans in any other, and there is no way for a desk to know which of its amendments has landed first. An amendment is put on the link against a sector that some desk currently holds.

An amendment is written into the sector plan only while there is still a live lease on that sector -- one that the clock has not yet run past. Writing adds the amendment to the plan rather than replacing the plan wholesale, so nothing already booked there is displaced by a write that was prepared against an older view. A lease the clock has run past is released and the sector goes back to being unheld.

Sector plans are tidied from time to time of amendments that were put on the link but never got booked; an amendment that has been booked is left exactly where it is. Once every amendment is booked the watch is quiet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every amendment that has been booked stands in exactly one sector plan, so a booked flight-plan change is never carried away by a later write, by a lease running out, or by a tidy-up.

ASSUME NoDesk \notin Desks

Clip(n) == IF n < Horizon THEN n ELSE Horizon

vars == <<amend, plan, lease, clock>>

    /\ amend \in [Amends -> [state : {"raised", "inflight", "booked"},
                             sect : Sectors \cup {NoDesk}]]
    /\ plan \in [Sectors -> SUBSET Amends]
    /\ lease \in [Sectors -> [holder : Desks \cup {NoDesk}, until : 0..Horizon]]
    /\ clock \in 0..Horizon

    /\ plan = [s \in Sectors |-> {}]
    /\ lease = [s \in Sectors |-> [holder |-> NoDesk, until |-> 0]]
    /\ clock = 0

\* A control desk takes a lease on a sector's flight plan.  Leases run out on
\* the clock so a desk that goes quiet cannot hold a sector for ever.
TakeLease(d, s) ==
    /\ lease[s].holder = NoDesk
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = [holder |-> d, until |-> Clip(clock + LeaseTicks)]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<amend, plan, clock>>

\* An amendment is put on the sector datalink.  The link reorders freely, so
\* amendments raised in one order can reach the plan in any other.

    /\ lease[s].holder # NoDesk
    /\ amend' = [amend EXCEPT ![a] = [state |-> "inflight", sect |-> s]]

<|start|>user<|message|>A vending machine network sells at prices pushed out from a regional desk. Only one desk holds pricing authority at a time, and authority moves between the desks by epoch: a desk takes it by claiming an epoch number strictly newer than any epoch yet claimed by anybody.

Taking authority makes every machine that is still carrying an older schedule stale, because a machine selling at a schedule the network has moved on from is exactly the case the operator has to avoid -- a superseded desk's prices in the field are unauthorised prices.

Only the desk that currently holds authority may push a schedule out, and a machine records the epoch it was loaded under when it takes one. A push from a desk that has been superseded carries an older epoch than the machine is already at and simply cannot land, so a stale desk cannot reprice the estate behind the current desk's back.

Machines in the field are not reliable. A single machine may lose its modem and drop off the network without saying so, after which it goes on carrying whatever schedule it last took and no push can reach it; the rest of the estate carries on being repriced normally.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A machine that is selling at the current schedule was loaded with exactly that schedule under exactly the epoch it is carrying, so no machine is ever selling on the authority of a desk the network has superseded.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every machine left stale by a change of pricing authority eventually catches up to the current schedule, unless it has dropped off the network altogether.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od13m3p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Machines, Desks, MaxEpoch, NoDesk

ASSUME NoDesk \notin Desks

Epochs == 1..MaxEpoch
Loads == [mach : Machines, ep : Epochs]

VARIABLES machine, claim, boss, loaded, bricked

vars == <<machine, claim, boss, loaded, bricked>>

Typing ==
    /\ machine \in [Machines -> [state : {"stale", "current"}, ep : 0..MaxEpoch]]
    /\ claim \in [Desks -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ boss \in [desk : Desks \cup {NoDesk}, ep : 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ loaded \subseteq Loads
    /\ bricked \subseteq Machines

Init ==
    /\ machine = [m \in Machines |-> [state |-> "current", ep |-> 0]]
    /\ claim = [d \in Desks |-> 0]
    /\ boss = [desk |-> NoDesk, ep |-> 0]
    /\ loaded = {}
    /\ bricked = {}

\* Price authority moves between the regional desks by epoch.  A desk claims an
\* epoch newer than any yet claimed by anybody.
Claim(d, e) ==
    /\ \A k \in Desks : e > claim[k]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![d] = e]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<machine, boss, loaded, bricked>>

\* Taking authority makes every machine still carrying an older price schedule
\* stale, so a machine cannot go on selling at a schedule the network has left.
TakeOver(d) ==
    /\ claim[d] > boss.ep
    /\ boss' = [desk |-> d, ep |-> claim[d]]
    /\ machine' = [m \in Machines |->
                     IF machine[m].ep < claim[d]
                     THEN [state |-> "stale", ep |-> machine[m].ep]
                     ELSE machine[m]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claim, loaded, bricked>>

\* Only the desk that currently holds authority may push a schedule, and the
\* machine records the epoch it was loaded under.  A push from a desk that has
\* been superseded carries an older epoch and simply cannot land.
Push(m) ==
    /\ boss.desk # NoDesk
    /\ m \notin bricked
    /\ machine[m].ep < boss.ep
    /\ machine' = [machine EXCEPT ![m] = [state |-> "current", ep |-> boss.ep]]
    /\ loaded' = loaded \cup {[mach |-> m, ep |-> boss.ep]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claim, boss, bricked>>

\* A single machine may lose its modem and go off the network without saying
\* so; it then carries whatever schedule it last had.
Brick(m) ==
    /\ bricked = {}
    /\ bricked' = {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<machine, claim, boss, loaded>>

Quiet ==
    /\ \A m \in Machines : machine[m].state = "current" \/ m \in bricked
    /\ \A d \in Desks : claim[d] = MaxEpoch \/ boss.ep = MaxEpoch
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Desks, e \in Epochs : Claim(d, e)
    \/ \E d \in Desks : TakeOver(d)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Push(m) \/ Brick(m)
    \/ Quiet

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E d \in Desks, e \in Epochs : Claim(d, e))
    /\ WF_vars(\E d \in Desks : TakeOver(d))
    /\ WF_vars(\E m \in Machines : Push(m))

\* A machine that is selling at the current schedule was loaded with exactly
\* that schedule under exactly the epoch it is carrying, so no machine is ever
\* selling on the authority of a desk the network has superseded.
NoStaleSchedule ==
    \A m \in Machines :
        (machine[m].state = "current" /\ machine[m].ep > 0) =>
            (Cardinality({x \in loaded : x.mach = m /\ x.ep = machine[m].ep}) = 1)

EveryMachineEventuallyCatchesUp ==
    \A m \in Machines :
        (machine[m].state = "stale") ~>
            (machine[m].state = "current" \/ m \in bricked)

====

<|start|>user<|message|>A hospital pharmacy destroys expired controlled drugs against a destruction book. The book is the legal record of what was denatured and when, and it is written through a single register carrying a revision number.

Witness benches are manned and stood down through the shift as staff move between duties, so the number of witnesses available to a destruction changes while the round is running. A destruction needs at least a set number of benches manned at the moment it happens.

A batch is drawn from the safe against the revision the destruction book currently carries. Destroying it is irreversible: the batch is denatured and gone, and the book entry can never be unwritten or amended. The write into the book is a compare-and-swap against the revision the batch was drawn on, and landing bumps that revision -- so a batch that was drawn twice, because it was put back and drawn again, cannot be written into the book twice.

A batch that cannot be destroyed on this pass -- because the book has moved on since it was drawn, or because there are not enough benches manned to witness it -- goes back into the safe intact and can be restocked and drawn again later. Once the register has been stamped for the last time in the round the safe is shut.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A batch that has been destroyed stands exactly once in the destruction book, however many times it was drawn from the safe and put back.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od16m7p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Batches, Benches, MinWitness, MaxRev

Entries == [btc : Batches, rev : 1..MaxRev]

VARIABLES batch, book, rev, manned

vars == <<batch, book, rev, manned>>

Typing ==
    /\ batch \in [Batches -> [state : {"stored", "drawn", "destroyed", "returned"},
                              base : 0..MaxRev]]
    /\ book \subseteq Entries
    /\ rev \in 0..MaxRev
    /\ manned \subseteq Benches

Init ==
    /\ batch = [b \in Batches |-> [state |-> "stored", base |-> 0]]
    /\ book = {}
    /\ rev = 0
    /\ manned = Benches

\* Witness benches are manned and stood down through the shift, so the number
\* of witnesses available to a destruction changes while the round is running.
StandDown(w) ==
    /\ w \in manned
    /\ manned' = manned \ {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batch, book, rev>>

ManUp(w) ==
    /\ w \notin manned
    /\ manned' = manned \cup {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batch, book, rev>>

\* A batch is drawn from the safe against the revision the destruction book
\* currently carries.
Draw(b) ==
    /\ batch[b].state = "stored"
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b] = [state |-> "drawn", base |-> rev]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, rev, manned>>

\* Destruction is irreversible: the batch is denatured and gone, and the book
\* entry can never be unwritten.  The write into the book is a compare-and-swap
\* against the revision the batch was drawn on, so a batch drawn twice cannot
\* be written twice; enough benches must also be manned to witness it.
Destroy(b) ==
    /\ batch[b].state = "drawn"
    /\ batch[b].base = rev
    /\ Cardinality(manned) >= MinWitness
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ book' = book \cup {[btc |-> b, rev |-> rev + 1]}
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b].state = "destroyed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED manned

\* A batch that cannot be destroyed on this pass -- the book has moved on, or
\* there are not enough witnesses -- goes back into the safe intact.
Return(b) ==
    /\ batch[b].state = "drawn"
    /\ \/ batch[b].base # rev
       \/ Cardinality(manned) < MinWitness
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b].state = "returned"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, rev, manned>>

Restock(b) ==
    /\ batch[b].state = "returned"
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b].state = "stored"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, rev, manned>>

Shut ==
    /\ rev = MaxRev
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Benches : StandDown(w) \/ ManUp(w)
    \/ \E b \in Batches : Draw(b) \/ Destroy(b) \/ Return(b) \/ Restock(b)
    \/ Shut

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A batch that has been destroyed stands exactly once in the destruction book,
\* however many times it was drawn from the safe and put back.
DestroyedOnce ==
    \A b \in Batches :
        (batch[b].state = "destroyed") =>
            (Cardinality({x \in book : x.btc = b}) = 1)

====

<|start|>user<|message|>An airport baggage router reads bags off a belt and drops them into chutes for their flights. The sorter's read queue is deliberately short: while it is full a bag simply stays on the belt and goes round again rather than being taken, which is the backpressure the pier relies on to keep the sorter from being swamped at a bank.

A bag taken off the belt goes under the read head. Reading a tag takes several looks -- the labels are creased, wet, or facing the wrong way -- and the readers here are slow but never fail: a bag may sit under the head for a long time before its tag finally resolves, but it always resolves in the end.

Dropping a bag into a chute is the irreversible step. Once the bag is over the lip it is in the cart and on its way to the aircraft; it cannot be pulled back, and it can never be dropped a second time. The drop is written onto the flight manifest as it happens, and that manifest is what the ramp loads against.

Chutes jam from time to time and a jammed chute takes nothing, but the pier is never worked with every chute jammed at once, and a jam is cleared and the chute goes back into use. Once every bag has been dropped the pier is quiet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A bag that has gone over a chute lip appears exactly once on the flight manifest, however long its tag took to read.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bag taken into the sorter's read queue is eventually dropped into a chute.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bags, Chutes, QueueCap, MaxScan

VARIABLES bag, queue, manifest, jammed

vars == <<bag, queue, manifest, jammed>>

Typing ==
    /\ bag \in [Bags -> [state : {"arriving", "queued", "scanning", "dropped"},
                         scans : 0..MaxScan]]
    /\ queue \subseteq Bags
    /\ manifest \subseteq [bag : Bags, chute : Chutes]
    /\ jammed \subseteq Chutes

Init ==
    /\ bag = [b \in Bags |-> [state |-> "arriving", scans |-> 0]]
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ manifest = {}
    /\ jammed = {}

\* The sorter's read queue is short.  While it is full a bag stays on the belt
\* and goes round again rather than being taken, which is the backpressure the
\* pier relies on to keep the sorter from being swamped.
Admit(b) ==
    /\ bag[b].state = "arriving"
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < QueueCap
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {b}
    /\ bag' = [bag EXCEPT ![b].state = "queued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, jammed>>

Pick(b) ==
    /\ bag[b].state = "queued"
    /\ bag' = [bag EXCEPT ![b].state = "scanning"]
    /\ queue' = queue \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, jammed>>

\* Reading a bag tag takes several looks.  Readers here are slow but never
\* fail: a bag may sit under the head for a long time before its tag resolves.

    /\ bag[b].scans < MaxScan
    /\ bag' = [bag EXCEPT ![b].scans = bag[b].scans + 1]

\* cart, and it can never be dropped a second time.  The drop is recorded on

    /\ Cardinality(jammed) + 1 < Cardinality(Chutes)
    /\ jammed' = jammed \cup {k}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bag, queue, manifest>>

Clear(k) ==
    /\ k \in jammed
    /\ jammed' = jammed \ {k}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bag, queue, manifest>>

<|start|>user<|message|>An air-traffic centre records coordination slips -- a climb clearance to be honoured, an agreement with the next centre -- against whichever band of airspace the traffic is in. A slip that has been committed is one the receiving controller has been told about: they work the traffic on it and never ask for it again, so a committed slip that ended up belonging to a band nobody is working would be an update lost in the worst possible place.

The centre re-sectorises during the watch, and each change carries a strictly newer epoch number. Bands are handed over between desks and split back out as traffic builds and thins, so the number of bands actually being worked changes while aircraft are in the air.

A slip is filed against a band somebody is currently working, and records the epoch the centre was configured under at the time. It is committed once it belongs to a band that is still being worked. Handing a band over carries every slip filed against it across to a band that stays worked, in the same movement as the handover itself, so nothing is stranded. Splitting a band back out puts it on a controller's desk again for new filings.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every committed coordination slip still belongs to a band that a controller is actually working, so no committed slip is stranded by a re-sectorisation.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every coordination slip that is raised is eventually committed.
<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od1m9p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Notes, Bands, MaxEpoch, NoBand

ASSUME NoBand \notin Bands

VARIABLES slip, owner, working, epoch

vars == <<slip, owner, working, epoch>>

Typing ==
    /\ slip \in [Notes -> [state : {"raised", "filed", "committed"},
                           ep : 0..MaxEpoch]]
    /\ owner \in [Notes -> Bands \cup {NoBand}]
    /\ working \subseteq Bands
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch

Init ==
    /\ slip = [n \in Notes |-> [state |-> "raised", ep |-> 0]]
    /\ owner = [n \in Notes |-> NoBand]
    /\ working = Bands
    /\ epoch = 0

\* A coordination slip is filed against a band that somebody is working, and
\* records the epoch the centre was configured under when it was filed.
File(n, b) ==
    /\ slip[n].state = "raised"
    /\ b \in working
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![n] = b]
    /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![n] = [state |-> "filed", ep |-> epoch]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<working, epoch>>

\* Committing a slip is what the receiving controller is told about; once told
\* they work the traffic on it and never ask for it again.
Commit(n) ==
    /\ slip[n].state = "filed"
    /\ owner[n] \in working
    /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![n].state = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, working, epoch>>

\* Re-sectorising under a strictly newer epoch.  Handing a band over carries
\* every slip filed against it to a band that stays worked, in the same
\* movement as the handover, so nothing is stranded in a band nobody has.
HandOver(b, c) ==
    /\ b \in working
    /\ c \in working
    /\ b # c
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ working' = working \ {b}
    /\ owner' = [n \in Notes |-> IF owner[n] = b THEN c ELSE owner[n]]
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1

<|start|>user<|message|>A library consortium deaccessions titles from its shared catalogue. Each branch keeps its own catalogue register carrying a revision number, and a branch marks a title for deaccession against the revision its register currently shows.

That check is what stops a title that was marked twice -- because a mark was dropped and taken again -- being pulped twice.

A mark that has gone stale, because the marking branch's register has moved on since, is dropped and the title simply stays on the shelf to be marked again later.

Branch catalogue nodes are not reliable. One branch's node may drop off the consortium without saying so; it then stops confirming anything, and a mark that was taken by that branch is dropped rather than left hanging. The remaining branches carry on deaccessioning normally.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A title that has been withdrawn stands exactly once in the deaccession register, however many branches marked it and however often it was marked and dropped.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every title marked for deaccession is eventually resolved, either withdrawn or put back on the shelf.

<|start|>user<|message|>A regional grid's load shedder pushes protection setpoints -- an under-frequency threshold, an overload trip level -- out to its substations. A setpoint that has been applied is written into that station's journal, and the protection relays read their behaviour back from that journal, so a setpoint that quietly vanished from a journal would be an update lost where it matters most.

The shedding scheme is re-run through the watch, and each re-run carries a strictly newer epoch number. A setpoint is drafted against the scheme epoch standing at the time, and is applied at a substation only under that same epoch. A setpoint drafted under a scheme that has since been superseded, and that nobody has pushed through, is dropped rather than applied, and can be redrafted against the current scheme later.

There is a privileged override: the control engineer may push a setpoint drafted under an older scheme through anyway when the grid is close to shedding and there is no time to redraft. The override still writes the setpoint into exactly one station journal, and there are only so many overrides in a shift.

Re-running the scheme carries the station journals across untouched: a new scheme changes what will be applied next, never what the relays are already holding. Station journals are separately tidied of setpoints that were drafted at them but never applied.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every applied setpoint stands in exactly one station journal, so no setpoint the relays are already holding is carried away by a re-scheme, an override, or a tidy-up.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

vars == <<entry, journal, epoch, forced>>

Typing ==
    /\ entry \in [Setpoints -> [state : {"draft", "applied", "dropped"},
                                ep : 0..MaxEpoch]]
    /\ journal \in [Stations -> SUBSET Setpoints]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ forced \in 0..ForceCap

Init ==
    /\ entry = [p \in Setpoints |-> [state |-> "draft", ep |-> 0]]
    /\ journal = [s \in Stations |-> {}]
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ forced = 0

\* A setpoint is applied at a substation only under the scheme epoch it was
\* drafted against; applying writes it into that station's journal, which is
\* what the protection relays read back.
Apply(p, s) ==
    /\ entry[p].state = "draft"
    /\ entry[p].ep = epoch
    /\ journal' = [journal EXCEPT ![s] = journal[s] \cup {p}]
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![p].state = "applied"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, forced>>

\* The privileged override: the control engineer may push a setpoint drafted
\* under an older scheme through anyway when the grid is close to shedding.
\* It still goes into exactly one station journal, and there are only so many
\* overrides in a shift.
Force(p, s) ==
    /\ entry[p].state = "draft"
    /\ entry[p].ep # epoch
    /\ forced < ForceCap
    /\ journal' = [journal EXCEPT ![s] = journal[s] \cup {p}]
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![p].state = "applied"]
    /\ forced' = forced + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

\* A setpoint drafted under a scheme that has since been superseded, and that
\* nobody has forced through, is dropped rather than applied.
Drop(p) ==
    /\ entry[p].state = "draft"
    /\ entry[p].ep # epoch
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![p].state = "dropped"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, epoch, forced>>

Redraft(p) ==
    /\ entry[p].state = "dropped"
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![p] = [state |-> "draft", ep |-> epoch]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, epoch, forced>>

\* Re-running the shedding scheme under a strictly newer epoch.  Journals are
\* carried across untouched -- a new scheme changes what will be applied next,
\* never what the relays are already holding.
Rescheme ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<entry, journal, forced>>

\* Station journals are tidied of setpoints that never got applied.
Tidy(s) ==
    /\ journal' = [journal EXCEPT ![s] =

    /\ UNCHANGED <<entry, epoch, forced>>

Steady ==
    /\ \A p \in Setpoints : entry[p].state = "applied"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Setpoints, s \in Stations : Apply(p, s) \/ Force(p, s)
    \/ \E p \in Setpoints : Drop(p) \/ Redraft(p)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Tidy(s)
    \/ Rescheme
    \/ Steady

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every applied setpoint stands in exactly one station journal, so no setpoint
\* the relays are already holding is carried away by a re-scheme, an override
\* or a tidy-up.
NoLostSetpoint ==
    \A p \in Setpoints :
        (entry[p].state = "applied") =>
            (Cardinality({s \in Stations : p \in journal[s]}) = 1)

A reroute goes live only if two things still hold: the revision it was drafted against is still the plan's standing revision, and the console that worked it up is itself still reading that revision. A console that has fallen behind the plan is a stale participant, and a reroute from a stale console is refused rather than pushed onto the belts -- pushing it would route bags on a picture of the pier that the router has already left behind. A refused reroute is voided and can be redrafted later.

Consoles catch up with the plan on their own schedule, each at its own pace. A reroute that goes live bumps the plan's revision and records which console pushed it. The pier settles once every reroute is live, or once the plan has been stamped for the last time in the bank.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every live reroute was pushed onto the belts exactly once, by a console that was up to date with the routing plan at the moment it went live, so nothing on the belts came from an operator the plan had already left behind.

<|start|>user<|message|>A regional grid's load shedder trips feeder breakers when the system runs short. Tripping a breaker is irreversible: the breaker latches open and only a linesman at the substation can reset it, so a feeder that has been tripped can never be tripped again, and a second trip order against it would simply be an error in the record.

Shedding agents take out leases on individual feeders rather than owning them outright. An agent takes a lease on a feeder nobody is holding, and the lease runs out on the clock rather than being held until the agent gives it up, because an agent that goes quiet would otherwise hold a feeder out of the scheme for the rest of the event.

Only an agent holding a live lease on a feeder -- one the clock has not yet run past -- may trip it, and the trip is written to the event log against that agent as it happens. An agent can release a lease early when it decides not to shed that feeder. A lease the clock has run past is reclaimed so another agent can take the feeder on, whether or not its holder is still answering.

Agents are not reliable. A single agent may lose its telemetry link and go quiet without saying so, after which it trips nothing further while its leases simply run out; the remaining agents carry on shedding.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A feeder that has been tripped was tripped exactly once, however many agents held a lease on it before or after, and however many of them went quiet.

Clip(n) == IF n < Horizon THEN n ELSE Horizon

vars == <<feeder, lease, trips, clock, dark>>

    /\ feeder \in [Feeders -> [state : {"closed", "tripped"},
                               by : Agents \cup {NoAgent}]]
    /\ lease \in [Feeders -> [holder : Agents \cup {NoAgent}, until : 0..Horizon]]
    /\ trips \subseteq [fdr : Feeders, agt : Agents]
    /\ clock \in 0..Horizon
    /\ dark \subseteq Agents

    /\ feeder = [f \in Feeders |-> [state |-> "closed", by |-> NoAgent]]
    /\ lease = [f \in Feeders |-> [holder |-> NoAgent, until |-> 0]]
    /\ trips = {}
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ dark = {}

\* out on the clock, so an agent that goes quiet cannot hold a feeder out of
\* the scheme for the rest of the event.
Take(a, f) ==
    /\ a \notin dark
    /\ lease[f].holder = NoAgent
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![f] = [holder |-> a, until |-> Clip(clock + LeaseTicks)]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<feeder, trips, clock, dark>>

    /\ a \notin dark
    /\ feeder[f].state = "closed"
    /\ lease[f].holder = a
    /\ lease[f].until > clock
    /\ feeder' = [feeder EXCEPT ![f] = [state |-> "tripped", by |-> a]]

    /\ UNCHANGED <<feeder, lease, trips, dark>>

<|start|>user<|message|>A print shop spooler keeps one shared record: the running page tally for the day, together with the set of jobs whose pages have already been folded into that tally. Job numbers run from one upward and a job's page count is its own number. The spooler runs under a configuration epoch that the shop may advance a bounded number of times; advancing the epoch is a reconfiguration and it deliberately leaves outstanding work alone. A clerk picks up a job that has not been folded in yet and for which no slip is already outstanding, and writes a slip recording the job, the tally value the clerk read, and the epoch that was current when the clerk read it. The shop only allows a bounded number of slips to be written in a day. A clerk redeems a slip only when the override is not engaged, the slip's epoch is still the current epoch, the tally has not moved since the clerk read it, and the job is still unfolded; redeeming writes back the value the clerk computed from what it read and marks the job folded. A slip whose epoch is stale, whose recorded tally no longer matches the record, or whose job has already been folded is torn up. The shop manager has a privileged override: engaging it blocks clerk redemptions, releasing it unblocks them, and while it is engaged the manager may fold any unfolded job into the tally directly, which also tears up every outstanding slip. SAFETY PROPERTY: The page tally always equals the sum of the page counts of exactly those jobs recorded as folded in, so no clerk's update is ever lost or double counted. LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever slips are outstanding, they are eventually all resolved -- redeemed or torn up -- so the slip board always empties again.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NumJobs, MaxEpoch, MaxSlips

ASSUME /\ NumJobs \in Nat /\ NumJobs >= 2
       /\ MaxEpoch \in Nat
       /\ MaxSlips \in Nat /\ MaxSlips >= 1

Jobs == 1 .. NumJobs

\* A job's page count is simply its job number.
RECURSIVE PageSum(_)
PageSum(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET j == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN j + PageSum(S \ {j})

TotalPages == PageSum(Jobs)

VARIABLES tally, folded, epoch, slips, override, budget

vars == <<tally, folded, epoch, slips, override, budget>>

Slips == [job : Jobs, base : 0 .. TotalPages, ep : 0 .. MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
    /\ tally \in 0 .. TotalPages
    /\ folded \subseteq Jobs
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ slips \subseteq Slips
    /\ override \in BOOLEAN
    /\ budget \in 0 .. MaxSlips

Init ==
    /\ tally = 0
    /\ folded = {}
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ slips = {}
    /\ override = FALSE
    /\ budget = MaxSlips

\* Reconfiguration advances the epoch and leaves outstanding slips behind.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ ~override
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, folded, slips, override, budget>>

Read ==
    /\ budget > 0
    /\ \E j \in Jobs \ folded :
        /\ \A s \in slips : s.job # j
        /\ slips' = slips \cup {[job |-> j, base |-> tally, ep |-> epoch]}
    /\ budget' = budget - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, folded, epoch, override>>

\* The clerk writes back the value it computed from what it read, so the
\* epoch-and-value check is the only thing standing between the shop and a
\* lost update.
Redeem ==
    /\ ~override
    /\ \E s \in slips :
        /\ s.ep = epoch
        /\ s.base = tally
        /\ s.job \notin folded
        /\ tally' = s.base + s.job
        /\ folded' = folded \cup {s.job}
        /\ slips' = slips \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, override, budget>>

Tear ==
    /\ \E s \in slips :
        /\ (s.ep # epoch \/ s.base # tally \/ s.job \in folded)
        /\ slips' = slips \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, folded, epoch, override, budget>>

Engage ==
    /\ ~override
    /\ override' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, folded, epoch, slips, budget>>

Release ==
    /\ override
    /\ override' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, folded, epoch, slips, budget>>

\* The manager's privileged fold invalidates every slip on the board.
AdminFold ==
    /\ override
    /\ \E j \in Jobs \ folded :
        /\ tally' = tally + j
        /\ folded' = folded \cup {j}
    /\ slips' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, override, budget>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure \/ Read \/ Redeem \/ Tear
    \/ Engage \/ Release \/ AdminFold

Spec == /\ Init
        /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ SF_vars(Redeem) /\ WF_vars(Tear) /\ WF_vars(Release)

\* The record and the fold set can never drift apart.
NoLostUpdate == tally = PageSum(folded)

SlipBoardDrains == (slips # {}) ~> (slips = {})

Cabins are numbered, and a cabin belongs to the line matching the parity of its number. Only cabins that are currently enrolled in service may take part. An enrolled cabin that has no route request outstanding may raise a request for a block that is not currently reserved, and only situations in which at most two route requests are outstanding at once are considered. An enrolled cabin turns its outstanding request into a reservation only while it is holding its own line's token and the requested block is still unreserved; the block then records that cabin as its holder and the request is cleared. A cabin may release a block it holds back to the pool at any time. ---- MODULE W4Od10m1p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NumCabins, NumBlocks, MaxOutstanding, NoCabin, NoBlock

ASSUME /\ NumCabins \in Nat /\ NumCabins >= 3
       /\ NumBlocks \in Nat /\ NumBlocks >= 1
       /\ MaxOutstanding \in Nat

Cabins == 0 .. NumCabins - 1
Blocks == 1 .. NumBlocks

\* The two line control instances run over the same ring of cabins and draw
\* their track blocks from the one shared pool.
Lines == {0, 1}
LineOf(c) == c % 2

VARIABLES token, enrolled, holder, request

vars == <<token, enrolled, holder, request>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in [Lines -> Cabins]
    /\ enrolled \subseteq Cabins
    /\ holder \in [Blocks -> Cabins \cup {NoCabin}]
    /\ request \in [Cabins -> Blocks \cup {NoBlock}]

Outstanding == Cardinality({c \in Cabins : request[c] # NoBlock})

Init ==
    /\ token = [l \in Lines |-> l]
    /\ enrolled = Cabins
    /\ holder = [b \in Blocks |-> NoCabin]
    /\ request = [c \in Cabins |-> NoBlock]

Advance(l) ==
    /\ token' = [token EXCEPT ![l] = (token[l] + 1) % NumCabins]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, holder, request>>

Ask(c) ==
    /\ c \in enrolled
    /\ request[c] = NoBlock
    /\ \E b \in Blocks :
        /\ holder[b] = NoCabin
        /\ request' = [request EXCEPT ![c] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, enrolled, holder>>

\* A cabin may only convert a request while it holds its own line's token.
Reserve(c) ==
    /\ c \in enrolled
    /\ token[LineOf(c)] = c
    /\ request[c] # NoBlock
    /\ holder[request[c]] = NoCabin
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![request[c]] = c]
    /\ request' = [request EXCEPT ![c] = NoBlock]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, enrolled>>

Free(c) ==
    /\ \E b \in Blocks :
        /\ holder[b] = c
        /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![b] = NoCabin]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, enrolled, request>>

\* Striking a cabin off the roll must also strip it of everything it holds.
Withdraw(c) ==
    /\ c \in enrolled
    /\ enrolled' = enrolled \ {c}
    /\ holder' = [b \in Blocks |->
                     IF holder[b] = c THEN NoCabin ELSE holder[b]]
    /\ request' = [request EXCEPT ![c] = NoBlock]
    /\ UNCHANGED token

Reinstate(c) ==
    /\ c \notin enrolled
    /\ enrolled' = enrolled \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, holder, request>>

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Lines : Advance(l)
    \/ \E c \in Cabins : Ask(c) \/ Reserve(c) \/ Free(c)
                          \/ Withdraw(c) \/ Reinstate(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Cabins may raise requests freely; the bound on how many route requests
\* are examined at once is what keeps the reachable state space small.
RequestBound == Outstanding <= MaxOutstanding

\* A block in the shared pool is only ever held by a cabin still in service.
NoWithdrawnHolder ==
    \A b \in Blocks : holder[b] # NoCabin => holder[b] \in enrolled

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of containers aboard the ships, stacked on the quays, and hanging on the spreaders always adds up to the number of containers the yard started with. LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever a container is hanging on a spreader, the yard eventually reaches a point where every spreader is clear again.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od7m3p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cranes, Berths, StartAboard, MaxFailures, NoLead

ASSUME /\ StartAboard \in Nat /\ StartAboard >= 1
       /\ MaxFailures \in Nat
       /\ NoLead \notin Cranes
       /\ Cardinality(Cranes) > Cardinality(Berths)

VARIABLES lead, inService, aboard, ashore, spreader, failures

vars == <<lead, inService, aboard, ashore, spreader, failures>>

TotalBoxes == StartAboard * Cardinality(Berths)

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN f[b] + Tally(f, S \ {b})

TypeOK ==
    /\ lead \in [Berths -> Cranes \cup {NoLead}]
    /\ inService \subseteq Cranes
    /\ aboard \in [Berths -> 0 .. TotalBoxes]
    /\ ashore \in [Berths -> 0 .. TotalBoxes]
    /\ spreader \in [Berths -> 0 .. 1]
    /\ failures \in 0 .. MaxFailures

Init ==
    /\ lead = [b \in Berths |-> NoLead]
    /\ inService = Cranes
    /\ aboard = [b \in Berths |-> StartAboard]
    /\ ashore = [b \in Berths |-> 0]
    /\ spreader = [b \in Berths |-> 0]
    /\ failures = 0

\* The berths are independent but the crane pool is shared, so a crane can
\* lead at most one berth at a time.
ElectAt(b) ==
    /\ lead[b] = NoLead
    /\ \E c \in inService :
        /\ \A o \in Berths : lead[o] # c
        /\ lead' = [lead EXCEPT ![b] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inService, aboard, ashore, spreader, failures>>

\* A crane can only be taken out of service with an empty spreader, so no
\* box is ever stranded by a failover.
Fail ==
    /\ failures < MaxFailures
    /\ \E c \in inService :
        /\ \A b \in Berths : lead[b] = c => spreader[b] = 0
        /\ inService' = inService \ {c}
        /\ lead' = [b \in Berths |->
                       IF lead[b] = c THEN NoLead ELSE lead[b]]
    /\ failures' = failures + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aboard, ashore, spreader>>

Restore ==
    /\ \E c \in Cranes \ inService : inService' = inService \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, aboard, ashore, spreader, failures>>

\* One straddle gang serves both berths, so only one spreader may be loaded
\* at a time even though the berths are otherwise independent.
LiftAt(b) ==
    /\ lead[b] \in inService
    /\ \A o \in Berths : spreader[o] = 0
    /\ aboard[b] > 0
    /\ aboard' = [aboard EXCEPT ![b] = aboard[b] - 1]
    /\ spreader' = [spreader EXCEPT ![b] = 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, inService, ashore, failures>>

LandAt(b) ==
    /\ lead[b] \in inService
    /\ spreader[b] = 1
    /\ spreader' = [spreader EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
    /\ ashore' = [ashore EXCEPT ![b] = ashore[b] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, inService, aboard, failures>>

ReloadAt(b) ==
    /\ ashore[b] > 0
    /\ ashore' = [ashore EXCEPT ![b] = ashore[b] - 1]
    /\ aboard' = [aboard EXCEPT ![b] = aboard[b] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, inService, spreader, failures>>

Land == \E b \in Berths : LandAt(b)

Next ==
    \/ Fail \/ Restore \/ Land
    \/ \E b \in Berths : ElectAt(b) \/ LiftAt(b) \/ ReloadAt(b)

Spec == /\ Init
        /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(Land)

\* Every box is aboard, ashore, or on a spreader -- never anywhere else.
BoxesConserved ==
    Tally(aboard, Berths) + Tally(ashore, Berths)
        + Tally(spreader, Berths) = TotalBoxes

SpreadersAlwaysClear ==
    (\E b \in Berths : spreader[b] = 1) ~> (\A b \in Berths : spreader[b] = 0)

====
